Keep contract liabilities (合同负债), project contract value, newly signed contracts, and major winning-bid disclosures (重大中标项目披露) as separate measures.
Do not assume that all contract liabilities are first-quarter project deposits, or that the absence of a major winning-bid announcement proves that no projects were obtained.

facts.statement: Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 301120 corresponds to Xin Te Electric Co., Ltd. (新特电气; 301120.SZ).

On June 10, 2026, Xin Te Electric Co., Ltd. (新特电气; 301120.SZ) stated that if it has a major winning-bid project meeting information-disclosure requirements, it will make timely disclosure on the information-disclosure platform designated by the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.

Contract liabilities (合同负债) represent consideration received or receivable from customers for which the company has not yet fulfilled the related performance obligations; they are not necessarily project deposits or total contract value.

A period-end contract-liability balance may relate to contracts signed in earlier periods and is affected by payment milestones, delivery and acceptance, performance progress, and the timing of revenue recognition.
The June 10, 2026 public response by Xin Te Electric Co., Ltd. (新特电气; 301120.SZ) did not disclose the specific project or customer composition of the first-quarter contract-liability balance.

dependencies.requirement: Attribute the June 10, 2026 disclosure-policy response to the issuer corresponding to code 301120.
Do not equate a period-end contract-liability balance with first-quarter new contract value, a single project deposit, or total project contract value.
Use the company's response only to establish its disclosure principle; do not treat it as evidence of the number, size, or composition of first-quarter projects.

answer_points.statement: The high contract-liability balance and the lack of a major winning-bid announcement are not inherently contradictory because they have different accounting, timing, and disclosure scopes.
Contract liabilities should not be described uniformly as project deposits and cannot, by themselves, establish total project contract value or first-quarter newly signed contract value.

A first-quarter period-end balance may include consideration from contracts signed before the first quarter and may remain outstanding because delivery, acceptance, performance, or revenue recognition has not yet occurred.

Only projects meeting the applicable information-disclosure threshold would necessarily generate a major winning-bid announcement; contract liabilities cover the broader set of relevant contracts at the reporting date.

The available information is insufficient to conclude that scattered projects erupted in the first quarter, and the absence of a major announcement does not prove that the company obtained no projects.

Determining the source of the balance would require the opening balance, current-period additions, revenue recognized or contract liabilities released, and the principal project and customer composition; the stated 'over RMB 80 million' historical high and 'one-fifth of annual revenue' comparison should not be treated as independently verified.

context_constraints.requirement: Evaluate the Indian 10-year bond with an 8% coupon and maturity date of 12-Nov-2020.
Treat INR 10,800 as the total remaining amount received at maturity, including any final coupon; exclude coupons already received from both alternatives.
Assume INR 9,750 is immediately realizable sale proceeds and ignore taxes, transaction costs, reinvestment income, and default risk.

facts.statement: The bond was purchased during the initial offer period for INR 5,000.
The bond can currently be sold for INR 9,750.
Under the stated cash-flow interpretation, total remaining proceeds at maturity on 12-Nov-2020 are INR 10,800.
Selling gain over the purchase price is INR 9,750 − INR 5,000 = INR 4,750, and the cumulative simple return is INR 4,750 ÷ INR 5,000 = 95%.
Holding gain over the purchase price is INR 10,800 − INR 5,000 = INR 5,800, and the cumulative simple return is INR 5,800 ÷ INR 5,000 = 116%.
The additional proceeds from holding instead of selling are INR 10,800 − INR 9,750 = INR 1,050, representing INR 1,050 ÷ INR 9,750 = 10.77% of the current sale value.

dependencies.requirement: Use the original purchase price and current sale proceeds to calculate the historical selling gain and cumulative return.
Use the original purchase price and total maturity proceeds to calculate the historical holding gain and cumulative return.
Use the current sale proceeds as the opportunity cost when calculating the incremental return from holding to maturity.
Interpret the 10.77% figure as a simple return over the remaining holding period only if INR 10,800 includes all remaining maturity cash flows.

answer_points.statement: Selling now produces INR 4,750 of gain over the INR 5,000 purchase price, or a 95% cumulative simple return.
Holding to maturity produces INR 5,800 of gain over the purchase price, or a 116% cumulative simple return, under the stated maturity-proceeds assumption.

For the decision today, the INR 5,000 purchase price is a sunk cost: holding gives up INR 9,750 today in exchange for INR 10,800 at maturity, an incremental simple return of 10.77% over the remaining period.
The 95% and 116% figures are cumulative simple returns, not annualized returns; annualization requires the exact current date and dated payment schedule.

Coupons already received should be added to both alternatives for a complete return since purchase. If INR 10,800 excludes remaining coupons, those coupons must be added and the dated cash flows should be compared using yield to maturity or present value.

The hold-versus-sell decision should also consider after-tax returns, accrued interest and clean-versus-dirty pricing, transaction costs, issuer credit risk, liquidity needs, and the return available from reinvesting INR 9,750.

numeric_targets.description: Cumulative simple return from selling now
Cumulative simple return from holding to maturity
Incremental simple return from holding rather than selling now

facts.statement: Junxin Co., Ltd. (军信股份; 301109.SZ) is the company associated with Shenzhen Stock Exchange security code 301109.

Junxin Co., Ltd. (301109.SZ) had a forward-adjusted closing price of RMB 16.397 on May 7, 2026 and RMB 13.34 on June 10, 2026; the available complete daily price series covered April 21, 2026 through June 10, 2026 and did not include a complete June 11, 2026 daily record.
Using the forward-adjusted closing prices for May 7, 2026 and June 10, 2026, the calculated decline was (RMB 16.397 − RMB 13.34) / RMB 16.397 = approximately 18.64%.
As of June 11, 2026, no concurrent index data was available to establish whether Junxin Co., Ltd.'s performance was inconsistent with the broader market.

As of June 11, 2026, no confirmed board resolution or formal announcement established that Junxin Co., Ltd. had decided to implement a share repurchase, or established an operating abnormality or a specific cause for the recent share-price decline.

dependencies.requirement: Attribute all price, operating, and repurchase conclusions to Junxin Co., Ltd. (301109.SZ), not to another security with a similar code.
Calculate and describe the decline only using the stated forward-adjusted closing-price dates; do not present the approximately 18.64% calculation as confirmation of the user's 22% figure.
Do not infer a complete June 11, 2026 closing-price movement from a dataset that ends with the June 10, 2026 complete daily record.

Treat the lack of index data and the lack of a confirmed operating, causal, or repurchase announcement as limits on what can be concluded, not as proof that the relevant event or condition does not exist.
Conclude that the price decline is supported by the stated observations, while operating difficulty, the specific cause of the decline, and inconsistency with the broader market remain unconfirmed.

answer_points.statement: The available evidence is insufficient to conclude that Junxin Co., Ltd. (301109.SZ) is experiencing operating difficulties or to identify a specific cause of the share-price decline; a decline in the share price alone does not establish abnormal operations.

The stock did decline materially from RMB 16.397 on May 7, 2026 to RMB 13.34 on June 10, 2026 on a forward-adjusted closing-price basis, but the available dates and price methodology do not precisely verify the stated 22% decline.
The claim that the stock underperformed the broader market cannot be verified because concurrent index data is unavailable.

This assessment is not an official response from Junxin Co., Ltd.'s board secretary.

facts.statement: Shenzhen Yingtang Intelligent Control Co., Ltd. (深圳市英唐智能控制股份有限公司) is the company corresponding to Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 300131.SZ.

On 2026-06-01, Shenzhen Yingtang Intelligent Control Co., Ltd. (300131.SZ) announced that it had received a Shenzhen Stock Exchange review inquiry letter (审核问询函) concerning its application for an acquisition through share issuance and cash consideration (发行股份及支付现金购买资产) and ancillary fundraising; the company stated that it would address the questions and submit a response, and the announcement did not announce rejection, termination, or obstruction of the transaction.

The adjusted daily closing prices of Shenzhen Yingtang Intelligent Control Co., Ltd. (300131.SZ) were RMB 16.79 per share on 2026-06-01, RMB 17.22 per share on 2026-06-02, and RMB 17.18 per share on 2026-06-03.

The adjusted closing price of Shenzhen Yingtang Intelligent Control Co., Ltd. (300131.SZ) rose from RMB 17.94 per share on 2026-05-26 to RMB 18.69 per share on 2026-05-27, and rose from RMB 16.79 per share on 2026-06-01 to RMB 17.22 per share on 2026-06-02.
The 2026-06-02 adjusted closing price increased by approximately 2.56% from 2026-06-01, calculated as (RMB 17.22 / RMB 16.79 - 1) × 100%.

dependencies.requirement: Attribute the review event and price data to 300131.SZ before drawing any conclusion.
Treat the review inquiry letter as a stage of regulatory review, not as evidence that the acquisition was rejected, terminated, or obstructed.
Use the transaction status together with the post-announcement and preceding price path; do not infer causation merely from temporal proximity.

answer_points.statement: As of the evaluation time, the available evidence does not establish that the recent decline in Shenzhen Yingtang Intelligent Control Co., Ltd. (300131.SZ)'s share price was caused by an obstructed acquisition.
The disclosed event was a Shenzhen Stock Exchange review inquiry letter, with the company intending to respond; it was not disclosed as a rejection, termination, or obstruction of the acquisition.

The first complete trading day after the 2026-06-01 disclosure saw the adjusted closing price rise by approximately 2.56%, followed by only a slight decline on 2026-06-03, so the post-disclosure pattern was not a continuous one-way fall.
The broader 2026-05-26 to 2026-06-03 price movement also included multiple rising trading days and therefore was not consecutively declining throughout the period.

The inquiry may have introduced uncertainty, but the available announcement and contemporaneous price evidence do not prove a causal relationship between the inquiry and the share-price decline or substantiate the premise that the acquisition was obstructed.

answer_points.statement: The available public evidence is insufficient to conclude that the combination of shareholder selling and private placement harmed minority investors, although potential dilution, conflicts of interest, pricing fairness, use of proceeds, disclosure, and approval procedures require verification.

Shareholder selling and private placement should be assessed separately: selling is generally a shareholder disposition, while private placement is a company financing arrangement that may dilute existing shareholders but does not by itself establish harm.

The share price showed a weak short- to medium-term condition under the stated rule: the June 25, 2026 closing price was below both the 20-day and 60-day simple moving averages, and it was lower than the May 7, 2026 closing price.
The observed price decline does not establish that shareholder selling or private placement caused the decline.

No publicly verifiable, specific, and executable plan to restore minority-investor confidence could be confirmed as of June 26, 2026; this does not prove that the company has no undisclosed or subsequently announced plan.

A proper assessment should verify the selling parties and their relationships with the company and placement recipients, selling and issuance quantities and timing, issue price and lock-up period, proceeds use and expected returns, dilution to earnings per share, net asset return and voting rights, related-party abstention, and regulatory approval; any confidence-building response should disclose responsible parties, scale, timing, conditions, funding source, and progress.

context_constraints.requirement: Assess the claim primarily for broad stock-market indexes, not for every individual stock or market episode.
Define “faster” explicitly, such as equal-percentage threshold-crossing time, peak-to-trough versus recovery duration, daily return magnitude, or asymmetric volatility.
Treat downside asymmetry as a statistical tendency rather than a universal rule; crisis rebounds can also be exceptionally rapid.

facts.statement: Historical broad equity-index returns commonly exhibit a heavier downside tail, volatility clustering, and larger subsequent volatility increases after negative returns than after comparable positive returns.
During stressed markets, synchronized selling, reduced liquidity, margin calls or forced deleveraging, and volatility-sensitive risk reductions can increase downward price pressure.
Loss aversion in prospect theory means that people generally experience an equivalent loss more intensely than a gain, increasing attention to, memory of, and responsiveness to market declines.
A 20% decline from an initial price requires a subsequent 25% gain from the reduced price to return to the initial price.

A 2015 discussion of the Chinese stock-market decline attributed the episode in part to broad leveraged participation and imperfect market mechanisms and risk controls, while disputing that the HOMS platform was the principal cause.

dependencies.requirement: State which definition of “faster” is being used, because threshold timing, drawdown and recovery duration, daily moves, and volatility can produce different conclusions.
Use the 2015 Chinese episode only as an illustration of possible leverage and market-mechanism contributions, not as proof of a universal cause of stock-market declines.
Use the percentage-base arithmetic to explain why recoveries can feel slower, without treating it as evidence that prices mechanically fall faster.

answer_points.statement: Yes, broad equity markets often show measurable downside asymmetry: large declines can be concentrated in shorter periods and negative returns are often associated with greater subsequent volatility, but declines are not universally faster than advances.

Faster declines can result from synchronized selling, deteriorating liquidity, leverage-driven margin calls or forced deleveraging, and risk-management feedback that reduces exposure after volatility rises.
These mechanisms are contributing explanations rather than a single universal cause of every crash.
Loss aversion does not fully explain the phenomenon, but it can magnify its perceived severity by making losses more salient, memorable, and likely to trigger rapid decisions.
A percentage loss requires a larger percentage recovery from the lower base, which can make a recovery appear especially slow even without an additional market mechanism.
The most accurate conclusion depends on the chosen speed definition, market, and period; the available 2015 China evidence is too narrow to establish a universal causal explanation.

context_constraints.requirement: The subject is Huazi Technology Co., Ltd. (华自科技股份有限公司), listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange under code 300490.SZ.
“Better gross margin” must be evaluated using a like-for-like comparison of gross margin or gross margin percentage, not merely order value, selling price, or geographic origin.

The comparison must distinguish expected margin at the order stage from actual gross margin recognized after revenue recognition, with consistent product configuration, delivery stage, cost allocation, and recognition period.

facts.statement: As of 2026-07-16, Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 300490 corresponds to Huazi Technology Co., Ltd. (华自科技股份有限公司; 300490.SZ).

As of 2026-07-16, Huazi Technology Co., Ltd. had not publicly disclosed a direct, like-for-like comparison of the gross margin or gross margin percentage of its European and domestic lithium-battery equipment orders.

dependencies.requirement: Use the absence of direct comparable disclosure to conclude that European orders being more profitable than domestic orders cannot be confirmed; do not infer that the margins are equal or that European margins are lower.

Do not treat order-stage expected margin as equivalent to realized gross margin after revenue recognition, and do not compare regions unless the relevant product, delivery, cost-allocation, and recognition-period definitions are consistent.

answer_points.statement: There is currently insufficient public, like-for-like evidence to confirm that Huazi Technology's landed European lithium-battery equipment orders have higher gross margins than its domestic orders.
The European origin of an order, its order value, or its selling price alone cannot establish that its gross margin is higher.
Order-stage expected margin may differ from the actual gross margin recognized when revenue is recorded.
A reliable regional comparison would require the same period and comparable product, delivery, cost-allocation, and revenue-recognition bases.
The prudent conclusion is that European order margins may differ, but their superiority over domestic order margins has not been verified.

context_constraints.requirement: The company must be identified as Qiangli XinCai (强力新材) (300429.SZ), the issuer associated with Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 300429.
Distinguish the convertible-bond conversion price from the separately referenced transfer price; the latter must be defined by the applicable agreement, announcement, or legal document.
Treat the reported price breach as a conditional premise only; do not infer that a downward conversion-price adjustment has been triggered without checking the applicable terms and procedures.

facts.statement: Shenzhen Stock Exchange security code 300429 corresponds to Qiangli XinCai (强力新材) (300429.SZ).

dependencies.requirement: The response must address Qiangli XinCai (强力新材), rather than another issuer, because the proposed compliance response depends on the correct entity.

Before assessing any consequence of the transfer price, identify its governing agreement or announcement and its precise contractual meaning; do not treat it as synonymous with the convertible-bond conversion price.

answer_points.statement: Qiangli XinCai should respond conditionally and should not promise price protection, guarantee a recovery in the share price, or intervene through undisclosed means.

A share price below the convertible-bond conversion price does not automatically cause the conversion price to be reduced. The company must first check the applicable prospectus terms, including trigger conditions, observation periods, adjustment limits, and required approval procedures.

Even if a downward-adjustment trigger is satisfied, the adjustment is generally not automatic. The company must make a decision in accordance with the applicable board, shareholder, and disclosure procedures, and may decide whether to propose an adjustment, its amount, and its implementation timing based on operating conditions, market conditions, and the interests of shareholders and bondholders.

The stated transfer price must be determined from the relevant agreement, announcement, or legal document. Without that definition, it is not possible to conclude that the company owes a price adjustment, compensation, repurchase, or other remedy.

A compliant response should state that the company will verify the applicable terms, perform the required decision-making and disclosure procedures, continue improving operations and information disclosure, and protect investors' lawful rights in accordance with law.

Without the relevant prospectus, announcements, transfer agreement, and verified price data, the response should not assert that a downward adjustment has already been triggered or that the company will undertake an adjustment, repurchase, or market-support action.

context_constraints.requirement: Use Tianqi Lithium Corporation (天齐锂业股份有限公司, 002466.SZ), the company corresponding to Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 002466.
Distinguish the April 2024 raw-material inventory disclosure from the FY2025 results and the latest disclosed Q1 2026 results.
Assess profitability using consolidated net profit attributable to shareholders and assess cost advantage as a relative operating-cost position, not as a guaranteed profit threshold.
Treat RMB 70,000–80,000 per tonne as a lithium carbonate futures-price scenario, not as Tianqi Lithium's realized selling price, inventory cost, or break-even price.

facts.statement: Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 002466.SZ corresponds to Tianqi Lithium Corporation (天齐锂业股份有限公司).

In its April 2024 response to the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, Tianqi Lithium stated that existing lithium concentrate inventory would be consumed gradually, causing the outbound cost to gradually approach the latest purchase price; it did not disclose a definite date for complete consumption.
Tianqi Lithium stated that it has a stable and cost-competitive supply of lithium concentrate, mature and stable lithium-chemical production processes, and relatively stable production costs.
For FY2025, Tianqi Lithium reported operating revenue of RMB 10.346 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 0.463 billion, and reported a return to profitability.
For Q1 2026, Tianqi Lithium reported operating revenue of RMB 5.128 billion, net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 1.876 billion, and a gross margin of 62.66%.

Tianqi Lithium controls the Greenbushes lithium mine and has an integrated lithium-resource and lithium-chemical business structure, supporting a relative cost advantage over companies that rely more heavily on purchased raw materials.

As of May 2026, Tianqi Lithium had not disclosed an official full cost stress test for a lithium carbonate price of RMB 70,000–80,000 per tonne, nor had a uniform comparable set of full costs and break-even points for peer companies been disclosed.

A lithium carbonate futures price is not the same metric as Tianqi Lithium's realized product selling price, lithium concentrate settlement price, inventory cost, or consolidated net profit attributable to shareholders.
RMB 0.463 billion and RMB 1.876 billion are both greater than zero; therefore, Tianqi Lithium was not loss-making on a net-profit-attributable-to-shareholders basis in FY2025 or Q1 2026.

dependencies.requirement: All operating, cost, and financial-performance evidence must refer to Tianqi Lithium Corporation rather than another lithium producer.
The current-profitability conclusion must use the latest reported full-year and quarterly realized results and must not be inferred solely from historical losses.
Interpret the inventory disclosure as gradual consumption and declining cost mismatch; do not convert it into a claim that all high-cost inventory had been consumed by early 2026.
Use resource ownership, supply structure, production integration, and cost stability to support only a relative cost advantage, not profitability at every lithium price.

Do not infer that a futures price of RMB 70,000–80,000 per tonne determines Tianqi Lithium's net profit; account for realized prices, raw-material settlement, inventory costs, missing stress tests, and peer cost comparability.

answer_points.statement: The evidence supports only that the impact of high-cost lithium concentrate inventory was being reduced gradually; it does not establish that the inventory had been fully consumed by early 2026. The earlier loss also cannot be attributed entirely to high-priced raw materials because pricing-cycle mismatch and other operating factors were involved.

Tianqi Lithium was not currently loss-making on the latest disclosed results: it reported positive attributable net profit in FY2025 and Q1 2026, so it was not in the same realized-profitability position as loss-making peers during those periods.
Tianqi Lithium still appears to have a relative cost advantage, supported by the Greenbushes resource, stable concentrate supply, and lithium-resource-to-chemical integration.

If lithium carbonate prices remained at RMB 70,000–80,000 per tonne for a prolonged period, Tianqi Lithium's profitability would likely be materially lower than in a high-price environment, but the available evidence cannot establish a precise break-even price.

A decline in lithium carbonate futures to RMB 70,000–80,000 per tonne cannot by itself prove that Tianqi Lithium would incur losses like most peers, because futures prices do not directly determine its realized sales prices, concentrate costs, inventory costs, or consolidated attributable net profit.

The appropriate conclusion is that Tianqi Lithium retains a relative cost-position advantage, but the available evidence is insufficient both to guarantee profitability at RMB 70,000–80,000 per tonne and to conclude that it would necessarily lose money like other companies.

context_constraints.requirement: Interpret Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 300173 as Funeng Dongfang Equipment Technology Co., Ltd. (福能东方装备科技股份有限公司), commonly referred to as Funeng Dongfang.
Keep company-level financing proceeds separate from cumulative cash dividends paid to all shareholders and from an individual investor's cost and returns.

Treat the payback calculation as a deliberately mechanical scenario: use 10 years as the minimum interpretation of 'more than ten years,' assume future dividends continue at the historical average rate, and ignore taxes, time value of money, share-count changes, and residual stock value.

facts.statement: Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 300173 corresponds to Funeng Dongfang Equipment Technology Co., Ltd. (福能东方装备科技股份有限公司).
The stated cumulative figures for Funeng Dongfang since listing, over more than ten years, are RMB 2.24 billion of financing and RMB 107 million of cash dividends.

On May 11, 2026, Funeng Dongfang stated that its comprehensive credit facilities were intended for daily production and operations, financing-structure optimization, lower financing costs, and improved capital-use efficiency, and that credit limits did not equal future actual financing.

Company financing is a funding transaction at the corporate level, whereas cumulative cash dividends are profit and cash distributions to shareholders collectively; neither amount is the same as one individual shareholder's investment or return.
Using RMB 2.24 billion divided by RMB 107 million, the cumulative financing-to-dividend ratio is 20.9345794393, approximately 20.93 times.
Using the approximately 20.93-times ratio and a 10-year period, the mechanical estimate is 20.9345794393 multiplied by 10, or approximately 209.3457943925 years.

dependencies.requirement: All company-specific conclusions must refer to the issuer corresponding to code 300173, not to another company.
Use the May 11, 2026 company response only to describe the stated purposes of comprehensive credit facilities; do not treat it as proof of the purposes or outcomes of all historical financing.
Do not infer an individual investor's payback period by directly comparing company-wide financing with dividends distributed to all shareholders.
The mechanical estimate must use the stated RMB 2.24 billion and RMB 107 million figures, the resulting 20.93-times ratio, and the explicit 10-year assumption.

answer_points.statement: Financing and dividends are different financial flows and are not required to be equal. Funeng Dongfang's public response gives operational and financing-management reasons for seeking credit, but it does not fully explain the purposes, deployment, or effectiveness of all five historical financing events.

The cumulative company-level financing and dividend figures cannot determine how many years a particular long-term investor needs to recover their investment, because they do not represent that investor's personal cost and returns.

Under the extreme mechanical assumptions, the figures imply approximately 20.93 ten-year periods, or 209.35 years; because the actual listing period exceeds ten years, a proportional estimate using the actual period would be longer. This is not a genuine individual payback period.

An individual payback calculation should use actual purchase cost and fees, after-tax dividends received, current shareholdings, and either current or sale value. If payback is measured only through future dividends, a specific assumption about future per-share dividends is also required.

numeric_targets.description: Mechanical payback estimate under the stated assumptions
Equivalent mechanical payback estimate under the stated assumptions

context_constraints.requirement: Interpret all company-specific claims as referring to Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Co., Ltd. (青海盐湖工业股份有限公司, 000792.SZ).

Distinguish the annual minimum cash-payout ratio, the three-year cumulative distribution requirement, the actual dividend payout ratio, and the proportion of cash dividends within total cash-and-stock dividends.
Interpret the 10% minimum as applying to the lesser of consolidated and parent-company distributable profit, not automatically to consolidated net profit attributable to shareholders.

facts.statement: Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Co., Ltd. (青海盐湖工业股份有限公司, 000792.SZ) is the company corresponding to Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 000792.

The 2025 Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Co., Ltd. Headquarters Profit Distribution Management Measures state that, absent special circumstances, the company should distribute cash dividends each year equal to at least 10% of the lesser of consolidated distributable profit and parent-company distributable profit for that year.

The 2025 Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Co., Ltd. Headquarters Profit Distribution Management Measures state that cash distributions over the latest three fiscal years should in principle be at least 30% of the average distributable profit for those three years.

The 2025 Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Co., Ltd. Headquarters Profit Distribution Management Measures define the 20%, 40%, and 80% differentiated figures as the ratio of cash dividends to total cash and stock dividends for the relevant distribution, rather than cash dividends divided by net profit.

Under the 2025 Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Co., Ltd. Headquarters Profit Distribution Management Measures, the specific distribution ratio is proposed by the board of directors and submitted to the shareholders' meeting for approval.
Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Co., Ltd.'s 2013 annual report recorded a proposed cash dividend of RMB 0.67 per 10 shares.

A 2024 report stated that Qinghai State-owned Assets Investment and Management Co., Ltd. held approximately 11.61% of Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Co., Ltd., was the controlling shareholder at that time, and that the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Qinghai Province was the actual controller.

dependencies.requirement: Use the 10% figure as an annual minimum cash-distribution constraint based on a specified distributable-profit scope; do not treat it as a fixed annual payout target or confuse the 20%, 40%, and 80% figures with net-profit payout ratios.

Assess whether the policy is conservative separately from whether actual long-term distributions are low; do not infer actual annual payout ratios from the policy minimum or from one historical dividend example.
Do not infer that a controlling shareholder's approximately 11.61% ownership caused low dividend willingness; ownership percentage alone does not establish dividend preferences or causation.

answer_points.statement: A 10% annual minimum cash-payout ratio is conservative and lower than a 30%-plus payout benchmark when the metrics and profit bases are comparable, but it does not mean Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Co., Ltd. can or will distribute only 10% each year.

The 10% requirement is a minimum constraint based on the lesser of consolidated and parent-company distributable profit; the actual ratio can be higher and is subject to board and shareholders' meeting approval.
The 20%, 40%, and 80% figures in the policy should not be compared directly with a 30% net-profit dividend payout ratio because they measure the cash component of total cash-and-stock dividends.

The available company-specific information does not establish that Qinghai Salt Lake Industry Co., Ltd.'s actual long-term payout ratio was only 10% or materially below peers; this requires a complete series of actual cash dividends, distributable profit or attributable net profit, and operating cash flow.

The approximately 11.61% ownership of the controlling shareholder does not by itself prove an unwillingness to pay higher dividends or establish that low ownership caused low dividends; such a conclusion would require company-specific evidence from dividend resolutions, shareholder voting, or funding arrangements.

A proper assessment should compare actual cash dividends with the relevant year's distributable profit, net profit attributable to shareholders, operating cash flow, capital expenditure, debt obligations, and subsequent funding needs.

context_constraints.requirement: Apply the analysis to Sinopharm Group Co., Ltd. (国药集团一致药业股份有限公司, 000028.SZ), also known as Sinopharm Accord (国药一致), rather than to another security with a similar name.

For the long-term below-book-value test, compare each closing price with the audited net assets per share attributable to ordinary shareholders for the most recent fiscal year.

facts.statement: In Sinopharm Accord's 2025-11-28 Valuation Enhancement Plan, Shenzhen Stock Exchange security code 000028 corresponds to Sinopharm Group Co., Ltd. (国药集团一致药业股份有限公司), commonly known as Sinopharm Accord (国药一致).

Under Sinopharm Accord's 2025-11-28 Valuation Enhancement Plan, the regulatory long-term below-book-value condition is that the stock's closing price is below the audited net assets per share attributable to ordinary shareholders for the most recent fiscal year on every trading day throughout 12 consecutive months.
When the condition in F3 is met, Sinopharm Accord is required to formulate a Valuation Enhancement Plan, submit it for board review, and disclose it.

dependencies.requirement: Apply all conclusions to Sinopharm Accord (000028.SZ), not to another company or security.
Do not treat the long-term below-book-value condition as the same metric as the company's unspecified Market Value Management System warning threshold.

Because the specific warning threshold is not disclosed, do not infer that a generic description of prolonged trading below book value triggers that threshold; if the complete F3 condition is met, identify the resulting obligation as formulation, board review, and disclosure of a Valuation Enhancement Plan.

answer_points.statement: Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 000028 is Sinopharm Group Co., Ltd. (Sinopharm Accord).

The specific numerical warning threshold in Sinopharm Accord's Market Value Management System cannot be reliably confirmed from the disclosed materials because the complete provision or a clear threshold was not stated.

Long-term below-book-value status requires the closing price to remain below the most recent fiscal year's audited net assets per share attributable to ordinary shareholders on every trading day for 12 consecutive months.

Satisfying that long-term condition triggers the obligation to formulate, obtain board review of, and disclose a Valuation Enhancement Plan; it does not, by itself, establish that an undisclosed specific warning threshold under the Market Value Management System has been triggered.

context_constraints.requirement: Identify Shenzhen Stock Exchange stock code 300352 as Beijing Beixinyuan Software Co., Ltd. (北京北信源软件股份有限公司), whose securities short name became ST Xinyuan (ST信源).
Distinguish the 2025 financial-report internal-control audit opinion from operating performance, solvency, and final delisting status.
Interpret “戴帽” as the implementation of an ST other-risk warning, and distinguish it from a delisting-risk warning and eventual termination of listing.

facts.statement: Shenzhen Stock Exchange stock code 300352 is Beijing Beixinyuan Software Co., Ltd. (北京北信源软件股份有限公司).
Beijing Beixinyuan Software Co., Ltd. was placed under an other-risk warning from May 6, 2026, and its securities short name changed from Beixinyuan (北信源) to ST Xinyuan (ST信源).
The company's auditor issued a qualified-as-negative opinion on its 2025 financial-report internal-control report, which was the disclosed direct basis for the other-risk warning.

Under the disclosed Shenzhen Stock Exchange rule, two consecutive fiscal years with an internal-control audit opinion of disclaimer or negative opinion, or failure to disclose the required internal-control audit report, may trigger a delisting-risk warning.

As of August 12, 2026, the disclosed status of Beijing Beixinyuan Software Co., Ltd. was an other-risk warning; the available facts did not confirm implementation of a delisting-risk warning or entry into final delisting proceedings.

Beijing Beixinyuan Software Co., Ltd. disclosed that its 2026 internal-control remediation was led by the chairman and included recurring special remediation meetings, implementation of a remediation plan, progress tracking, coordination of key difficulties, and optimization of the internal-control system.
The disclosed remediation actions did not establish by August 12, 2026 that the internal-control deficiencies had been eliminated or that remediation had produced measurable financial improvement.
Beijing Beixinyuan Software Co., Ltd.'s adjusted closing price was RMB 7.19 per share on April 29, 2026, RMB 5.75 on May 6, 2026, RMB 4.60 on May 7, 2026, and RMB 2.51 on August 11, 2026.

The available information did not provide a sufficiently complete continuous multi-year series of revenue, net profit, cash flow, and related operating metrics for Beijing Beixinyuan Software Co., Ltd.

dependencies.requirement: Use the company identity, ST effective date, and 2025 internal-control audit opinion together to support the conclusion that the company has already been placed under an ST other-risk warning and why.

Keep other-risk warning, delisting-risk warning, and final termination of listing as separate regulatory stages; do not treat the existing ST status or a potential second-year trigger as proof of imminent or certain delisting.

Assess the next-step risk conditionally: continuation of the relevant internal-control audit problem into a second consecutive fiscal year may lead to a delisting-risk warning, but does not itself establish final delisting.
Use the disclosed remediation actions to support that corrective work has begun, while requiring subsequent defect removal and audit verification before concluding that remediation succeeded.

Treat the price decline and the incomplete operating-data record separately from regulatory triggers; do not infer continuous operating deterioration or delisting solely from the share-price movement.

answer_points.statement: Stock code 300352 has already been “capped”: Beijing Beixinyuan Software Co., Ltd. became ST Xinyuan and entered an other-risk warning on May 6, 2026.
The direct trigger was the negative internal-control audit opinion for 2025, not merely a falling share price or weak general operating performance.

There is no sufficient basis as of August 12, 2026 to say that the company is already in delisting proceedings or will certainly be delisted. A second consecutive year of the relevant internal-control audit problem could, however, trigger a delisting-risk warning.

The company has undertaken chairman-led internal-control remediation, but the disclosed actions do not yet prove that the deficiencies have been fully corrected or that financial performance has improved.

The share price declined materially from late April to August 11, 2026, but price weakness alone cannot determine ST treatment, delisting-risk treatment, or final delisting; the available data also do not establish continuous deterioration in operating performance.
The key follow-up indicators are completion and verification of internal-control remediation and the opinion issued on the 2026 financial-report internal-control audit.

Compare FY2025 with Q1 2026.
Assess each segment using revenue and gross profit or gross margin, while treating consolidated revenue and profit as separate company-wide metrics.
Do not substitute consolidated company results for segment-level revenue or gross-profit data.

facts.statement: Qingdao Kingking Co., Ltd. (青岛金王, 002094.SZ) reported Q1 2026 consolidated operating revenue of RMB 339 million, up 4.78% year over year.

dependencies.requirement: Apply the reported figures only to Qingdao Kingking Co., Ltd. (青岛金王, 002094.SZ).
Use the consolidated figures to establish company-wide revenue growth with declining profitability, not to infer performance of any individual segment.

Because comparable segment revenue and gross-profit data are unavailable and the investor question is not quantitative operating evidence, do not identify any one of the three segments as the main drag.
Conclude that Q1 2026 showed consolidated growth in revenue but deterioration in reported profitability, while withholding segment-level attribution.

answer_points.statement: No reliable, complete, and comparable FY2025-to-Q1 2026 revenue or gross-profit change can be reported for Beauty Brand Operations, Online Agency Operations, or Cross-Border Supply Chain.
Q1 2026 consolidated performance was characterized by higher revenue but lower net profit and especially lower net profit excluding non-recurring items.
The available evidence is insufficient to determine whether Beauty Brand Operations, Online Agency Operations, or Cross-Border Supply Chain was the main drag on overall performance.

The overall profit decline cannot, on the available evidence, be attributed specifically to segment revenue contraction, gross-profit compression, business mix changes, or non-segment factors such as expenses, investment gains, or impairment.

Assess the buyback plan's validity, implementation status, remaining authorization, terms, purpose, and any disclosed reason for non-continuation; do not infer management motives from the share price alone.

facts.statement: As of 2026-07-16 06:39 UTC, Shenzhen-listed securities code 002202.SZ corresponds to Xinjiang Goldwind Science & Technology Co., Ltd.
As of 2026-07-16 06:39 UTC, no verifiable public announcement by Xinjiang Goldwind Science & Technology Co., Ltd. establishes why it did not continue repurchasing shares.

dependencies.requirement: State that the reason for non-continuation and the current plan status cannot be confirmed, rather than attributing a motive or asserting that the plan is active, completed, terminated, or has unused capacity.

A buyback plan generally authorizes purchases within specified conditions rather than requiring continuous purchases; a depressed share price alone does not automatically require further buying.

The appropriate verification is the latest buyback progress announcement, buyback report, or exchange disclosure, focusing on the implementation period, price ceiling, funding limits, purpose, remaining amount, and subsequent arrangements.

If repurchased shares are expressly intended for cancellation and are actually cancelled, total shares outstanding can decrease; this does not guarantee a higher share price or stronger shareholder confidence.

dependencies.requirement: Use the price data and disposal announcement only for Gangdi Jishu (港迪技术), 301633.SZ.
Treat the disclosed share quantities and percentages as disposal-plan caps, not as completed sales or proof of continuous selling.
Use the representative prices, the presence of recoveries, and the moving-average comparison to support a medium-term decline without describing the stock as falling every trading day.
Use the disposal announcement to establish disclosed intent and limits only; do not use it alone to infer the shareholders' operating-confidence or motives.

context_constraints.requirement: The calculation concerns the ABC security position.

Interpret five old shares becoming one new share as a 1-for-5 reverse stock split, with no fees, taxes, fractional-share adjustments, or other cost-basis changes.

facts.statement: The investor holds 500 shares of ABC at an average cost of USD 25 per share, and every five old shares become one new share.
ABC is stated to trade at USD 9 per share before the split and USD 45 per share after the split.
The pre-split total cost basis is 500 shares × USD 25 per share = USD 12,500.
The post-split share count is 500 shares ÷ 5 = 100 shares.
The post-split average cost is USD 25 per share × 5 = USD 125 per share.
The post-split market value is 100 shares × USD 45 per share = USD 4,500.
The unrealized gain or loss is USD 4,500 market value − USD 12,500 cost basis = negative USD 8,000.

dependencies.requirement: Use the 1-for-5 reverse-split ratio to convert the 500-share holding into 100 shares.
Treat average cost per share as the unchanged total cost basis divided by the post-split share count; do not confuse it with market price.
Calculate post-split market value using the post-split share count and the stated USD 45 market price.
Distinguish market value of USD 4,500 from the negative USD 8,000 unrealized loss.

answer_points.statement: The transaction is a 1-for-5 reverse stock split.
After the split, the position is 100 shares with an average cost of USD 125 per share.
At the stated post-split price of USD 45 per share, the position is worth USD 4,500.
The total cost basis remains USD 12,500, so the unrealized loss is USD 8,000; USD 8,000 is not the market value.

Peer companies' favorable earnings preannouncements alone do not establish that Shanghai Fullhan Microelectronics Co., Ltd. was late or noncompliant in disclosure; the applicable preannouncement triggers and formal reporting schedule must be checked.

answer_points.statement: The policy is directionally positive for Unisplendour Corporation Limited's switch and router businesses because basic, integrated, and high-capacity network construction can require such equipment; however, the available evidence is insufficient to conclude that the company will benefit significantly in orders or profits.

High-end AI data-center switches and core routers can have relatively high technical barriers, but ordinary access and campus equipment has lower barriers, and the available evidence does not support describing the entire switch and router portfolio as high-margin.

By total industry or investment scope, the new-generation communications network is larger than the AI data-center switch market because it covers four broad network categories and related construction, operations, and applications; the two markets are not directly comparable without harmonizing their definitions.

AI data-center switches have a more direct product fit and potentially more concentrated short- to medium-term earnings sensitivity for Unisplendour Corporation Limited, but existing evidence does not establish that they will contribute more to company performance than the broader new-generation communications-network opportunity.

facts.statement: For the proposed 2020 portfolio, the stated allocations are 30% U.S. equity through Fidelity Total Market Index Fund (FSKAX) or Fidelity ZERO Total Market Index Fund (FZROX), 15% developed international equity through Fidelity International Index Fund (FSPSX), 10% emerging-markets equity through Fidelity Emerging Markets Index Fund (FPADX), 15% inflation-protected U.S. Treasuries through Fidelity Inflation-Protected Bond Index Fund (FIPDX), 15% nominal U.S. Treasuries through Fidelity Intermediate Treasury Bond Index Fund (FUAMX), and 15% real estate.
For the proposed 2020 portfolio, 30% + 15% + 10% + 15% + 15% + 15% equals 100% of the portfolio.
For the proposed 2020 portfolio, U.S. equity, developed international equity, and emerging-markets equity total 30% + 15% + 10% = 55% of the portfolio.
For the proposed 2020 portfolio, TIPS and nominal U.S. Treasuries total 15% + 15% = 30% of the portfolio.
For the proposed 2020 portfolio, FSKAX and FZROX provide substantially overlapping broad U.S.-equity exposure, and a broad U.S. total-market fund already owns publicly traded real-estate companies.
For the proposed 2020 portfolio, nominal U.S. Treasuries and TIPS provide high-credit-quality government-bond exposure but remain exposed to interest-rate movements.

For the proposed 2020 portfolio, an exchange-traded fund (ETF) and an index mutual fund are investment wrappers rather than separate asset classes; replacing an index mutual fund with an ETF tracking the same market does not by itself add asset-class diversification.
For the proposed 2020 portfolio, a broad REIT fund, an individual REIT, and physical property have materially different concentration, liquidity, leverage, and cost risks.

dependencies.requirement: Use the stated allocation weights and grouped arithmetic to describe the portfolio as 100% invested, with 55% broad equity, 30% Treasuries, and 15% real estate.

Assess diversification and aggressiveness by treating REIT exposure as equity-like, recognizing the intentional real-estate overweight and overlap with total-market equity, and accounting for interest-rate risk in both Treasury categories.
Recommend choosing either FSKAX or FZROX rather than holding both, because their broad U.S.-equity exposures substantially overlap.

Evaluate whether ETFs are needed based on wrapper features such as automation, exact-dollar investing, trading flexibility, portability, costs, spreads, and possible taxable-account tax efficiency, not as an additional asset class.

Condition the diversification and suitability conclusions on identifying the exact real-estate vehicle and on the investor's time horizon, liquidity needs, loss tolerance, account type, and broader financial position.

answer_points.statement: The allocation is broadly diversified across asset classes, but it is simpler than it appears: 55% is broad equity, 30% is U.S. Treasury exposure, and 15% is real estate.

If the 15% real-estate allocation is a REIT investment, it behaves more like equity than bonds and creates a deliberate real-estate overweight because broad U.S. equity already includes publicly traded real-estate companies. The exact real-estate vehicle must be identified before assessing its concentration, liquidity, leverage, and cost risks.

The portfolio is conditionally moderate to moderately aggressive rather than extremely aggressive: the 30% Treasury allocation moderates risk, while equity and REIT exposures can still suffer substantial losses. Whether it is appropriate depends on the investment horizon, liquidity needs, emergency savings, other assets and debts, property exposure, account type, and ability to remain invested during a major decline.

Continuing regular purchases through 2020 can be sensible if the target allocation fits the investor's long-term plan, but no schedule should be selected on the assumption that 2020 returns are predictable. Set target weights and rebalancing bands, contribute regularly, direct new money toward underweight categories, and review periodically rather than reacting to every market move. Regular investing does not prevent losses or guarantee superior returns.

ETFs are not necessary merely for diversification. An inexpensive index mutual fund that supports automatic recurring investments and exact-dollar purchases may be preferable; ETFs may offer intraday trading, portability, and sometimes lower costs or greater tax efficiency in taxable accounts, but they also involve bid-ask spreads and can encourage unnecessary trading.

The most important next step is to identify the exact real-estate investment and decide whether a 15% real-estate overweight is intentional, then confirm that the overall risk level fits the investor's horizon and loss tolerance.

facts.statement: Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 000050 corresponds to Tianma Microelectronics Co., Ltd. (000050.SZ; 深天马A).

In October 2024, the People's Bank of China, the National Financial Regulatory Administration, and the China Securities Regulatory Commission established the stock repurchase and shareholding-increase relending program; an eligible listed company must satisfy Article 8 of the Listed Company Share Repurchase Rules, must not be subject to delisting-risk warning, and must have formally disclosed a repurchase plan.

Under the October 2024 relending notice, the loan must be included in the bank's unified credit assessment, the bank must independently assess repayment capacity, the funds must be used exclusively for the approved purpose through a dedicated securities account under closed operation, and the loan amount is subject to a prescribed proportion of the repurchase funds.

Tianma Microelectronics Co., Ltd.'s 2025 tracking-rating report states that its total profit turned positive in 2025 and that, from 2023 through March 2026, the company headquarters and its major subsidiaries Xiamen Tianma and Wuhan Tianma repaid loan principal and interest on schedule without delayed payments.

dependencies.requirement: Apply all financial and policy analysis to Tianma Microelectronics Co., Ltd. (000050.SZ), not to another company or shareholder.

Do not treat improved profitability or timely debt service as a complete test of capacity for RMB 3 billion of new debt; separately assess interest-bearing debt, cash flow, liquidity, capital expenditure, maturities, and interest coverage.

Treat the relending policy as a potential application channel subject to eligibility, disclosure, bank underwriting, dedicated-account controls, and loan-size limits; do not treat central-enterprise status or a below-book-value share price as automatic loan approval.

Separate legal and policy availability from financial feasibility: policy eligibility and a positive debt-service record do not by themselves establish that a one-time RMB 3 billion debt-funded repurchase is prudent.

answer_points.statement: There is a legal and policy path to study or apply for repurchase financing, but the available evidence does not support concluding that Tianma Microelectronics can prudently incur RMB 3 billion of new debt for a one-time share repurchase.

A nearly RMB 10 billion reduction in total liabilities, even if verified, does not by itself demonstrate RMB 3 billion of additional borrowing capacity because the reduction may involve operating liabilities rather than interest-bearing debt and may coincide with lower cash, asset contraction, or continuing investment needs.

The company's improved 2025 profitability and timely debt service are positive considerations, but a complete assessment still requires current unrestricted cash, operating cash flow, capital expenditure, debt maturities, interest coverage, net assets, market capitalization, price-to-book ratio, and the proportion of the proposed loan to available credit.

Being a central enterprise or trading below book value does not automatically make the company eligible for or entitled to a loan, and below-book-value trading does not automatically establish that debt-funded repurchases create shareholder value.

The decision should pass repayment-capacity, transaction-scale, repurchase-value, and compliance/governance tests, including assessment of operating cash flow after capital expenditure and debt maturities, minimum cash reserves, repayment terms, repurchase-price discipline, approval procedures, and bank underwriting.

A more prudent structure is an overall borrowing cap with staged execution, linked to cash flow, capital expenditure, leverage, and a predetermined repurchase-price limit, rather than committing immediately to the full RMB 3 billion.

As of August 19, 2026, Ronglian Technology Group Co., Ltd. had not publicly disclosed the amount of revenue recognized during January–June 2026 for the National Customs Information Center project.

As of August 19, 2026, Ronglian Technology Group Co., Ltd. had not publicly disclosed whether the Export-Import Bank of China and Dalian Commodity Exchange (大连商品交易所) intelligent-computing projects generated recognized revenue during January–June 2026 or the amounts involved.
As of August 19, 2026, Ronglian Technology Group Co., Ltd. had not publicly disclosed clear first-half 2026 revenue and gross-margin figures together with comparable first-half 2025 figures.
For the three months ended March 31, 2026, Ronglian Technology Group Co., Ltd. reported revenue of RMB 231 million, up 34.50% year over year.

dependencies.requirement: All project and financial conclusions must be attributed to Ronglian Technology Group Co., Ltd. (002642.SZ), not to another issuer.
Do not treat the RMB 79.505 million customs-project award as revenue recognized; project revenue conclusions must require explicit delivery, acceptance, accounting, or company disclosure evidence.
A first-half year-over-year improvement judgment requires comparable first-half revenue and gross-margin data; do not extrapolate the first-quarter revenue result to the full first half.

answer_points.statement: Security code 002642 corresponds to Ronglian Technology Group Co., Ltd.

The June 8, 2026 customs-project award confirms a contract win, not completion, delivery, or revenue recognition; the amount of revenue recognized in the first half of 2026 cannot be confirmed from the available disclosure.

The available disclosure also does not establish whether the Export-Import Bank of China and Dalian Commodity Exchange intelligent-computing projects generated first-half 2026 revenue or the amounts recognized.

It is not possible to determine whether first-half 2026 revenue or gross margin improved year over year because clear first-half 2026 and first-half 2025 comparable figures were not publicly disclosed.
The first-quarter 2026 revenue increase cannot be used as a proxy for full first-half performance and does not establish any gross-margin improvement.

The project revenue-recognition status and year-over-year revenue and gross-margin comparison should be verified against the company's formal 2026 interim report, announcement, or explicit investor-relations response.

context_constraints.requirement: The target is the issuer corresponding to Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 300374; data attributed to Hengtong Shares (恒通股份) must not be substituted for the target issuer.
Interpret “the first quarter” as the first quarter of 2026.

Distinguish gross profit, an RMB amount equal to revenue minus cost of revenue, from gross margin, a percentage equal to gross profit divided by revenue; “15 points,” “16 points,” and “9 points” denote gross-margin percentages.
Use a company-wide consolidated basis for comparison; if “core business” covers multiple segments, assess the segments separately rather than treating the company-wide margin as a segment margin.

facts.statement: Hengtong Shares (恒通股份) is not the issuer corresponding to Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 300374.
Hangxiao Steel Structure Co., Ltd. (杭萧钢构) reported first-quarter 2026 main-business revenue of RMB 1.308 billion and a gross margin of 15.3%.
Gross profit equals operating revenue minus operating cost, and gross margin equals gross profit divided by operating revenue.

dependencies.requirement: Verify that any financial data used for the answer belongs to the issuer corresponding to code 300374; do not use Hengtong Shares data for that issuer.

A gross-profit amount or gross-margin calculation for the target requires the target issuer’s same-period revenue and operating-cost figures; do not infer either metric from an unrelated issuer or from a margin stated for another company.
Use Hangxiao Steel Structure’s 15.3% figure as a gross-margin comparison, not as a gross-profit amount, and do not compare it with an unverified figure under a different accounting scope.

answer_points.statement: The available evidence is insufficient to reliably state the first-quarter 2026 gross-profit amount or gross margin of the issuer corresponding to Shenzhen code 300374, because Hengtong Shares must not be confused with that issuer.

Gross profit is an amount calculated as revenue minus operating cost, whereas gross margin is a percentage calculated as gross profit divided by revenue; therefore, the cited 15-point, 16-point, and 9-point figures are margins rather than gross-profit amounts.
The verifiable comparison figure is Hangxiao Steel Structure’s first-quarter 2026 gross margin of 15.3%, based on main-business revenue of RMB 1.308 billion.

There is no sufficiently verified basis here to confirm the cited first-quarter gross margins of 16% for Tubaobao (兔宝宝) and 9% for China State Construction (中国建筑), or to perform a reliable four-company comparison.

A reliable answer for code 300374 should disclose first-quarter 2026 operating revenue, operating cost, gross-profit amount, and consolidated gross margin; if the company has multiple core-business segments, it should also disclose each segment’s revenue, gross profit, and gross margin.

context_constraints.requirement: The analysis concerns Anhui Yingli Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (安徽英力电子科技股份有限公司; 300956.SZ).
Assess the status as of the 2026 interim-report period, using the reported loss in 2026 Q1 only as background for profit sensitivity.
Distinguish asset disposal, transfer or continued holding, depreciation, impairment, held-for-sale classification, one-time expensing, and the resulting profit impact.

facts.statement: Anhui Yingli Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (安徽英力电子科技股份有限公司; 300956.SZ) stated that it would no longer conduct photovoltaic business as a separate business.
Anhui Yingli Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (300956.SZ) reported a loss for the 2026 first quarter.

As of 2026-08-12, Anhui Yingli Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (300956.SZ) had not provided a confirmed disclosure establishing whether the photovoltaic-related plants and equipment had been disposed of, transferred, impaired, or expensed in full, nor confirming their treatment in the 2026 interim report.

For Anhui Yingli Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (300956.SZ) in the 2026 interim reporting period, property, plant and equipment that has reached the ready-for-use condition is generally depreciated over its useful life; construction in progress is generally not depreciated before reaching that condition; idle capacity may indicate impairment but does not by itself establish impairment; and disposal intent alone does not establish held-for-sale classification.

dependencies.requirement: Use the absence of confirmed company disclosure to conclude that the actual disposal and impairment status cannot be verified; do not present any specific treatment as confirmed.
Distinguish cessation of a separate photovoltaic business from derecognition of the related assets, and distinguish depreciation, impairment, held-for-sale accounting, and one-time expensing.

Assess continuing profit pressure conditionally: if the assets remain held, are not fully impaired, and are not subject to held-for-sale treatment, depreciation and other holding costs may continue; do not infer a specific loss amount from the 2026 Q1 loss.

answer_points.statement: It cannot currently be confirmed that the photovoltaic-related plants and equipment have been sold, transferred, impaired, or expensed in full, or that the 2026 interim report has disclosed a definitive treatment.
The decision not to conduct photovoltaic business separately does not mean that the related assets have automatically disappeared from the balance sheet or been fully charged to expense.

If the plants and equipment remain held, have reached the ready-for-use condition, and have not been fully impaired or classified as held for sale, depreciation and potentially maintenance or other holding costs may continue. Idle capacity alone does not require a full impairment charge.

A later disposal below carrying value could create a disposal loss, while transfer to another use, leasing, or disposal proceeds could reduce the continuing burden. An impairment charge, if supported by recoverable-value testing, could reduce current profit but also reduce the future depreciation base.

Because Anhui Yingli Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (300956.SZ) was already loss-making in 2026 Q1, any continuing depreciation, maintenance cost, or impairment could be more material relative to its thin profit base; however, the amount and inevitability of any further loss cannot be determined from the available facts.

The 2026 interim report should be checked for property, plant and equipment and construction-in-progress balances, current-period depreciation, impairment losses and provisions, held-for-sale assets, disposal gains or losses, transfers or leasing, and related maintenance or personnel costs.

context_constraints.requirement: Interpret Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 300274 as Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd. (阳光电源股份有限公司) and distinguish the company from its chairman.
Assess the one-year stock-price comparison using the available trading-day endpoints from 2025-07-29 to 2026-07-27.
Distinguish a chairman's buyback proposal from board approval and implementation, and use adjusted daily closing prices for the stock-performance comparison.
Express buyback amounts in RMB and stock prices in RMB per share.

facts.statement: Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 300274 corresponds to Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd. (阳光电源股份有限公司).
On 2026-07-21, Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd. received a share-buyback proposal from its chairman, Cao Renxian.

The 2026-07-21 proposal contemplated using the company's own or self-raised funds to repurchase RMB ordinary A shares through centralized bidding on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, with total funding of at least RMB 500 million and no more than RMB 1 billion, for future use in equity incentives or an employee share ownership plan.
The 2026-07-21 announcement stated that the proposed buyback could be implemented only after completing the required approval procedures and that uncertainty remained.
As of 2026-07-28, Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd. had no confirmed publicly disclosed buyback implementation timetable, and board approval of the proposal had not been confirmed.
Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd.'s adjusted closing price was RMB 73.81 per share on 2025-07-29.
Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd.'s adjusted closing price was RMB 116.21 per share on 2026-07-27.
Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd.'s adjusted closing price reached RMB 204.71 per share on 2025-11-06.
RMB 116.21 per share is RMB 42.40 higher than RMB 73.81 per share, so the available one-year endpoint comparison is positive rather than negative.
RMB 116.21 per share is RMB 88.50 lower than RMB 204.71 per share, showing a substantial decline from the 2025-11-06 stage high to 2026-07-27.

dependencies.requirement: Apply all buyback and price facts to Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd. (300274.SZ), not to another company or to the chairman personally.

Use the proposal, its terms, approval condition, and lack of a confirmed timetable together to conclude that a buyback proposal process has started, but board approval and implementation cannot be confirmed.

Use adjusted daily closing prices and distinguish the one-year endpoint comparison from the later decline from the stage high; do not treat the stage-high drawdown as proof of a negative one-year return.
Use the endpoint comparison to reject the claim that the stock had an overall negative one-year performance.
Use the stage-high comparison only to support the qualified statement that the stock experienced a substantial subsequent decline.

answer_points.statement: Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd. has initiated a buyback proposal process through a formal proposal from its chairman.

The proposal covers an RMB 500 million to RMB 1 billion A-share buyback funded with the company's own or self-raised funds, implemented through centralized bidding, and intended for equity incentives or an employee share ownership plan.
As of 2026-07-28, the proposal still required the relevant approval procedures; board approval, an accelerated board review, and a definite implementation timetable could not be confirmed.

The claim that the stock had an overall negative return over the preceding year is not supported by the available adjusted closing-price endpoints: RMB 116.21 on 2026-07-27 exceeded RMB 73.81 on 2025-07-29.

The stock nevertheless fell substantially from the RMB 204.71 adjusted closing price on 2025-11-06 to RMB 116.21 on 2026-07-27; these data alone do not establish the number of advances versus declines or prove that the company will expedite board consideration.

The decisive evidence for further progress is the company's formal board resolution, detailed buyback plan, and subsequent buyback-progress announcements; the chairman's proposal is not an implementation commitment.
