context_constraints.requirement: Interpret all company disclosures as referring to Wenzhou Hongfeng Co., Ltd. (温州宏丰) (300283.SZ), including its relevant hard-alloy materials business.
Distinguish the 2026 first-quarter inventory discussion, the unfinished 2026 second quarter, and the company's investor-interaction response dated 2026-04-21.
Keep product gross margin, inventory-strategy effects, product prices, production capacity, revenue, and actual sales volume as separate metrics.

facts.statement: Shenzhen Stock Exchange-listed security 300283 corresponds to Wenzhou Hongfeng Co., Ltd. (温州宏丰).
As of 2026-06-07, Wenzhou Hongfeng Co., Ltd. (温州宏丰) had not publicly disclosed a direct, quantified impact of recent silver-price volatility on its product gross margin.

As of 2026-06-07, Wenzhou Hongfeng Co., Ltd. (温州宏丰) had not publicly confirmed that its copper and silver inventory levels were reasonable or that this inventory strategy would stabilize subsequent earnings; disclosed information did not provide the relevant inventory-turnover, procurement-pricing, or hedging data.

In its 2026-04-21 investor-interaction response, Wenzhou Hongfeng Co., Ltd. (温州宏丰) stated that growth in revenue and improvement in gross margin for its hard-alloy materials business were jointly driven by higher major raw-material prices positively affecting revenue scale, steadily rising hard-alloy capacity, and continued cost reduction and efficiency improvements.

As of 2026-06-07, the second quarter of 2026 had not ended, and Wenzhou Hongfeng Co., Ltd. (温州宏丰) had not publicly disclosed that its hard-alloy products had been repriced upward or that sales volume had increased concurrently during that quarter.

dependencies.requirement: Apply the margin, inventory, and hard-alloy conclusions to Wenzhou Hongfeng Co., Ltd. (温州宏丰) and its relevant business disclosures, not to another issuer using a similar description.
Limit conclusions about second-quarter price and sales changes to the 2026-06-07 status, when the quarter was still incomplete.
Do not treat raw-material price effects on revenue, capacity growth, or cost reduction as proof of end-product price increases or actual sales-volume growth.

Express the silver-margin effect, inventory-strategy effect, second-quarter price change, and second-quarter sales growth as not yet confirmable; do not infer that any of these events did not occur merely because direct disclosure was unavailable.

answer_points.statement: The issuer corresponding to 300283.SZ is Wenzhou Hongfeng Co., Ltd. (温州宏丰).

The specific effect of recent silver-price volatility on product gross margin cannot currently be confirmed. The effect would also depend on procurement timing, inventory cost, product pricing, and the degree of cost pass-through, so silver-price movements alone do not establish a gross-margin change.

The view that copper and silver inventories are reasonable and will support stable earnings is an investor interpretation, not a conclusion confirmed by the available company disclosures; the necessary inventory and risk-management data are insufficient.
As of 2026-06-07, neither a second-quarter 2026 price increase for hard-alloy products nor concurrent sales-volume growth can be confirmed.

The company attributed earlier hard-alloy materials revenue growth and gross-margin improvement to higher major raw-material prices, rising capacity, and cost reduction and efficiency initiatives, but this statement does not by itself prove end-product price increases or actual sales-volume growth.

context_constraints.requirement: Analyze Yunnan Tin Co., Ltd. (Yunnan Tin, 锡业股份; 000960.SZ), not another tin-related issuer.
Use the single-day bulk-trade and market data for June 3, 2026, and treat forward-looking observations as conditional rather than established facts.
Keep institutional dedicated-seat net buying distinct from main-force capital net flow; they are different statistical measures and must not be treated as directly offsetting amounts.
Express prices in RMB per share, cash amounts in RMB million, and returns, discounts, turnover, and ratios as percentages.

facts.statement: On June 3, 2026, bulk trades in Yunnan Tin Co., Ltd. (000960.SZ) were executed at RMB 40.69 per share, while the stock closed at RMB 43.75 per share.
On June 3, 2026, institutional dedicated seats recorded net buying of approximately RMB 26.4485 million in Yunnan Tin Co., Ltd. (000960.SZ), and the main sellers were brokerage branch seats.
On June 3, 2026, Yunnan Tin Co., Ltd. (000960.SZ) rose 1.3%, had a turnover rate of 8.97%, and recorded main-force capital (主力资金) net outflow of approximately RMB 90.1366 million.
Using the June 3, 2026 prices, the bulk-trade discount was (RMB 43.75 − RMB 40.69) / RMB 43.75 = 6.9943%, or approximately 6.99%.
The institutional dedicated-seat net-buying amount divided by the main-force capital net-outflow amount was RMB 26.4485 million / RMB 90.1366 million = 29.3427%, or approximately 29.34%.

dependencies.requirement: Use the bulk-trade and closing prices to establish the approximately 6.99% discount and assess RMB 40.69 as a market reference price.
Use the 29.34% figure only as a scale comparison; do not interpret institutional dedicated-seat net buying as directly cancelling 29.34% of main-force capital net outflow.

Base the assessment of seller dominance, short-term price pressure, and the distribution-versus-washout conclusion on the combined discount, seat structure, institutional buying, turnover, price change, and capital-flow data rather than on any single indicator.

answer_points.statement: The transaction pattern shows some institutional absorption, but the approximately RMB 26.4485 million institutional net buying was limited relative to the approximately RMB 90.1366 million main-force capital net outflow; with brokerage branch seats as the main sellers, the overall pattern remains seller-dominated.

The approximately 6.99% discount creates a lower price reference and potential supply overhang. The stock's 1.3% gain on the same day does not by itself demonstrate that the bulk trades were bullish, given the high 8.97% turnover and substantial main-force capital outflow.

RMB 40.69 should be treated as an important price reference and a potential, not confirmed, support level. Repeated tests followed by recovery above it without abnormal volume would support effective absorption; a high-volume break and sustained closes below it would weaken that interpretation.

Key medium-term indicators are whether subsequent bulk-trade discounts narrow, whether declines become volume-amplified, whether rebounds have effective volume support, whether turnover normalizes, and whether main-force capital outflows narrow or turn into net inflows.

If forced to choose between distribution (出货) and a washout (洗盘), the current evidence leans slightly toward distribution or staged realization by sellers, but a single day's data are insufficient to confirm that classification.

A stable price above RMB 40.69, narrower subsequent discounts, less selling pressure, and continued institutional absorption would strengthen the washout or effective-absorption interpretation; a high-volume break below RMB 40.69, wider discounts, and continuing capital outflows would strengthen the distribution interpretation.

context_constraints.requirement: The subject is Jiawei New Energy Co., Ltd. (珈伟新能源股份有限公司, commonly 珈伟新能; 300317.SZ).
Assess April, May, and June 2026 separately; June 2026 is assessed only through June 25, 2026, and is not a completed month.
Assess year-over-year changes in electricity trading volume and separately assess whether any change was attributed to the El Niño effect.
Use electricity trading volume as the target metric and do not substitute generation volume or grid-connected electricity volume.

facts.statement: Jiawei New Energy Co., Ltd. (珈伟新能源股份有限公司, commonly 珈伟新能) is associated with Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 300317.SZ.
As of June 25, 2026, Jiawei New Energy Co., Ltd. had not announced verifiable April 2026 electricity trading volume and year-over-year data.
As of June 25, 2026, Jiawei New Energy Co., Ltd. had not announced verifiable May 2026 electricity trading volume and year-over-year data.
June 2026 was incomplete as of June 25, 2026, and Jiawei New Energy Co., Ltd. had not announced verifiable year-over-year electricity trading-volume data for that month.
As of June 25, 2026, Jiawei New Energy Co., Ltd. had not announced that changes in its April-to-June 2026 electricity trading volume were caused by the El Niño effect.
Electricity trading volume, grid-connected electricity volume, and electricity generation volume are distinct metrics and are not interchangeable.

dependencies.requirement: All monthly evidence and conclusions must concern Jiawei New Energy Co., Ltd. (300317.SZ), not another issuer.
Use the separate evidence status for April, May, and the incomplete June period; do not treat June 25 information as a full-month June result.
Do not infer an El Niño causal effect without an explicit company attribution or other direct causal evidence.
Do not use generation volume or grid-connected electricity volume as a proxy for electricity trading volume when assessing year-over-year growth.

answer_points.statement: Year-over-year growth in Jiawei New Energy's electricity trading volume cannot be confirmed for April 2026.
Year-over-year growth in Jiawei New Energy's electricity trading volume cannot be confirmed for May 2026.
Year-over-year growth in Jiawei New Energy's electricity trading volume cannot be confirmed for June 2026; moreover, June was not complete as of June 25, 2026.
The available evidence does not establish that any April-to-June 2026 change in electricity trading volume was caused by the El Niño effect.
Even if a year-over-year increase were later verified, the increase alone would not establish El Niño as its cause.
These conclusions are limited to the verifiable company information available as of June 25, 2026 and do not assert that the company has never made a relevant disclosure.

context_constraints.requirement: Analyze Dong-Ejiao Co., Ltd. (Dong-E 阿胶; 000423.SZ), the company corresponding to Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 000423.
Define summer as June through August; treat 2026 as an incomplete summer observation period because the available data end on 2026-05-29.
Use consistently adjusted daily closing prices for historical comparisons, and do not mix them with unadjusted quoted prices.

facts.statement: For Dong-Ejiao Co., Ltd. (000423.SZ), the analyzed adjusted daily-price series covers 2020-06-02 through 2026-05-29, with prices denominated in RMB per share.
Dong-Ejiao Co., Ltd. (000423.SZ) had an adjusted closing price of approximately RMB 20.90 per share on 2020-06-15 and approximately RMB 35.83 per share on 2020-08-31.
Dong-Ejiao Co., Ltd. (000423.SZ) had an adjusted closing price of approximately RMB 26.31 per share on 2021-06-02 and approximately RMB 19.98 per share on 2021-07-28.
Dong-Ejiao Co., Ltd. (000423.SZ) had adjusted closing prices between approximately RMB 46.83 and RMB 48.38 per share on 2025-08-25 through 2025-08-29.
Dong-Ejiao Co., Ltd. (000423.SZ) had an adjusted closing price of approximately RMB 48.65 per share on 2026-05-29, and 2026 did not yet provide a complete June-August observation period.

A July 2025 Xueqiu investor article discussed Dong-Ejiao's share-price decline in connection with perceived first-quarter operating slowdown, capital withdrawal from Chinese medicine stocks, institutional style shifts, and consumption concerns; these were investor views rather than formal company determinations.
Dong-Ejiao Co., Ltd. (000423.SZ) announced participation in the Shenzhen Stock Exchange 2025 annual collective earnings briefing on 2026-05-21 through video and graphic-text broadcasting.
As of 2026-06-01, Dong-Ejiao Co., Ltd. (000423.SZ) had not announced a specific share-price stabilization program or quantified market-cap enhancement plan in the referenced information.

dependencies.requirement: Assess the alleged recurring summer pattern only with the same June-August period, adjusted-price methodology, and observation boundary; do not combine adjusted and unadjusted prices.

Treat liquidity, institutional trading, operating expectations, and consumption concerns as market interpretations rather than evidence that any one factor was the principal cause or a company-confirmed explanation.
Describe the earnings briefing as a confirmed investor-communication action, while not presenting it as proof of a specific share-price stabilization or quantified confidence-restoration plan.

answer_points.statement: The claim that Dong-Ejiao's share price returned to the RMB 40-plus range every summer for six consecutive years is not supported: 2020 and 2021 are clear counterexamples, while late summer 2025 did enter that range.
The available price history does not establish a stable industry-seasonality pattern, and the incomplete 2026 observation period cannot be used to validate a six-year rule.

Investor commentary mentioned liquidity, institutional positioning, operating-growth expectations, and consumption conditions, but the available evidence does not identify any one of them as the dominant cause and does not show that management formally attributed the volatility to one of these factors.

The negative holding experience is genuine, but it does not by itself prove a fixed summer effect; changes in the price center, operating expectations, and valuation environment may affect perceived long-term investor returns and confidence.

The confirmed management action was participation in the 2026-05-21 Shenzhen Stock Exchange earnings briefing, which improves investor communication; no specific, quantified market-confidence restoration or share-price stabilization plan is confirmed.

context_constraints.requirement: Treat Hengxin Shenghuo (恒鑫生活) (301501.SZ) as the supplier under review, and do not equate price changes by downstream brands such as Heytea, Mixue, or Guming with a price change by Hengxin Shenghuo.
Separate the downstream pricing scenario beginning on May 22, 2026 from Hengxin Shenghuo's latest reported financial period, the first quarter of 2026.
Distinguish supplier ex-factory price execution, revenue, net profit attributable to shareholders, and PLA degradable-cup orders or market share.
Use Hengxin Shenghuo's consolidated operating revenue and net profit attributable to shareholders of the listed company when assessing financial protection.

facts.statement: On April 27, 2026, Hengxin Shenghuo (恒鑫生活) (301501.SZ) stated that it had a mature and flexible market-based pricing mechanism and used product lightweighting, structural optimization, and centralized procurement with price locking to offset raw-material cost pressure; the response did not announce an implemented price increase or specify its timing, customers, magnitude, or order execution.

In the first quarter of 2026, Hengxin Shenghuo (恒鑫生活) (301501.SZ) reported RMB 4.5 billion of operating revenue, up 7.5% year over year, and RMB 0.32 billion of net profit attributable to shareholders of the listed company, down 60.55% year over year.
A 2026 research report attributed Hengxin Shenghuo's first-quarter 2026 profit decline to lower sales gross margin, higher raw-material costs, foreign-exchange losses, and increased selling expenses.

The first-quarter 2026 financial data for Hengxin Shenghuo (恒鑫生活) (301501.SZ) precede May 22, 2026, and as of June 9, 2026 the company had not published a formal financial report covering the operating impact after May 22, 2026.

On April 27, 2026, Hengxin Shenghuo (恒鑫生活) (301501.SZ) stated that its core products were primarily green, low-carbon bio-based products, that fluctuations in petrochemical feedstock prices had limited direct cost impact on those core products, and that crude-oil price fluctuations could promote industry-wide green upgrading.

As of June 9, 2026, Hengxin Shenghuo (恒鑫生活) (301501.SZ) had not disclosed post-May 22, 2026 PLA-cup incremental orders or sales, the actual price gap between PLA cups and conventional plastic cups, customer material substitution, or an updated PLA-cup market-share change.

dependencies.requirement: Treat a market-based pricing mechanism as pricing capacity only; confirmation of synchronized price increases requires disclosure of executed increases and relevant timing, customers, magnitude, or orders.
Use first-quarter 2026 data to describe pre-May 22 operating performance, but do not use it to verify or attribute the effect of the May 22 downstream price changes.

Use the possible relative-price advantage of PLA cups only as a conditional business rationale; without disclosed orders, substitution, or share data, do not conclude that Hengxin Shenghuo's PLA-cup market share increased.

answer_points.statement: As of June 9, 2026, public disclosures did not confirm that Hengxin Shenghuo had synchronized its prices with the downstream brands; having a market-based pricing mechanism does not establish that a price increase had been implemented.

Hengxin Shenghuo's first-quarter 2026 revenue increased, but its net profit attributable to shareholders fell sharply; therefore, revenue growth did not translate into synchronized profit growth in that period.

The first-quarter data do not cover the May 22, 2026 price changes, and there was no formal financial disclosure by June 9, 2026 showing that those changes protected Hengxin Shenghuo's subsequent revenue or net profit.

Higher conventional plastic-cup prices could theoretically narrow the price gap with PLA cups and support green-material substitution, but there was no public evidence by June 9, 2026 that Hengxin Shenghuo's PLA-cup orders, sales, or market share had increased.

context_constraints.requirement: Analyze SF Holding Co., Ltd. (002352.SZ) as the investor and J&T Global Express Limited as the investee; do not treat the two companies as the same entity.
Assess the effect in SF Holding's consolidated financial statements.
Distinguish effects on investment carrying value, profit or loss, other comprehensive income, total equity, and impairment losses.

dependencies.requirement: Apply all conclusions to Shenzhen H&T Intelligent Control Co., Ltd. (002402.SZ), not to another company using a similar name.

Do not treat attributable net profit, non-recurring-item-adjusted attributable net profit, and operating cash flow as interchangeable indicators; the larger decline in adjusted profit signals weaker earnings quality while improved operating cash flow provides a countervailing consideration.

Acknowledge the consecutive share-price declines, but do not use share-price performance alone to establish operating difficulty or identify its sole cause.

The reported profit decline was materially affected by foreign-exchange losses, higher raw-material costs, delayed cost pass-through, and a sharp year-over-year increase in financing expenses.
The consecutive share-price declines are relevant market-risk signals, but they cannot by themselves prove that the company is experiencing operating difficulty or a going-concern crisis.

The appropriate conclusion is that the company has evident or potentially stage-specific operating pressure, but the cited 2026 interim results are insufficient to conclude that it has already fallen into severe operating difficulty, funding stress, or a continuing-operational crisis.

Further assessment should focus on subsequent non-recurring-item-adjusted profit, operating cash flow, financing expenses, receivables, inventories, short-term borrowings, and the ability to pass higher raw-material costs through to customers.

context_constraints.requirement: Define millionaire status as reaching EUR 1,000,000 in nominal liquid financial assets.
Assume contributions are made at each year-end and report the number of full years until the target is reached.
Use a EUR 0 starting balance, a constant EUR 50,000 annual salary, constant returns of 0%, 2%, or 6%, and exclude taxes, fees, inflation, and salary growth from the illustration.

facts.statement: The scenario concerns an individual living in France with an annual salary of EUR 50,000, a starting balance of EUR 0, and a nominal wealth target of EUR 1,000,000.
The compared savings rates are 15% and 40%, and the compared constant annual return assumptions are 0%, 2%, and 6%.
Saving 15% of EUR 50,000 produces an annual contribution of EUR 7,500, while saving 40% produces an annual contribution of EUR 20,000.
With EUR 7,500 contributed at each year-end, EUR 1,000,000 is reached after 134 full years at 0%, 66 years at 2%, or 38 years at 6%.
With EUR 20,000 contributed at each year-end, EUR 1,000,000 is reached after 50 full years at 0%, 36 years at 2%, or 24 years at 6%.
The 6% annual return is a hypothetical long-term investment-return assumption involving volatility and is not guaranteed deposit interest.

dependencies.requirement: Use the stated salary and savings rates to derive the annual contributions before calculating accumulation timelines.
Apply the timelines to a nominal liquid-financial-asset target; do not automatically count property, pension rights, or other assets.
Keep the 0%, 2%, and 6% cases distinct and do not present the 6% investment assumption as a guaranteed savings-account rate.
Use the calculated timelines and the risk qualification to support a conditional conclusion about whether investing is practically necessary.

answer_points.statement: Investing is not mathematically mandatory: a person could reach EUR 1,000,000 through savings alone if contributions were sufficiently high and the time horizon sufficiently long.
For a EUR 50,000 salary, saving 15% entirely in cash would require about 134 years at a 0% return, so it would not realistically reach the target during one working career.
At a constant 2% return, contributing EUR 7,500 annually would still require about 66 years, while contributing EUR 20,000 annually would require about 36 years.
Saving 40% materially shortens the timeline, but EUR 20,000 per year may be unrealistic if the EUR 50,000 salary is gross rather than net.
A hypothetical 6% return makes compound growth more important, but it represents risky long-term investing with possible negative years rather than a guaranteed American deposit rate.

Therefore, investing is probably necessary to reach EUR 1,000,000 in liquid financial assets within a normal working career without an exceptionally high savings rate or substantially higher income; the illustration is nominal and is materially affected by inflation, taxes, fees, salary growth, account structure, and the treatment of property or pension rights.

Annual contribution at a 40% savings rate

Years to reach EUR 1,000,000 with EUR 7,500 annual contributions at 2% return
Years to reach EUR 1,000,000 with EUR 7,500 annual contributions at 6% return
Years to reach EUR 1,000,000 with EUR 20,000 annual contributions at 0% return
Years to reach EUR 1,000,000 with EUR 20,000 annual contributions at 2% return

facts.statement: Huicheng Environmental Protection Co., Ltd. (惠城环保; 300779.SZ) reported 2025 first-three-quarter revenue of RMB 870 million, attributable net profit of RMB 30 million, and net cash flow from operating activities of negative RMB 140 million.

dependencies.requirement: Use the negative operating cash flow and the missing debt-maturity and liquidity data to avoid asserting a specific current repayment source; assess unrestricted cash, future operating collections, refinancing capacity, maturities, and remaining project spending instead.

Calculate historical ROE from attributable net profit divided by average attributable equity on the consolidated-company basis; do not treat 200,000 tons per year as an ROE denominator or as realized profit.

Treat 200,000 tons per year as design waste-processing capacity rather than saleable output or realized throughput, and do not derive a precise project net profit without the missing operating, price, and cost assumptions.

Separate existing catalyst, hazardous-waste, and three-waste businesses from the waste-plastics project; evaluate oil-price sensitivity through product-price and input-cost spreads rather than assuming a fixed one-directional effect.

answer_points.statement: Debt is ultimately repaid with cash, not nominal production capacity or accounting profit. The available information does not establish exactly how each debt obligation will be repaid; the key tests are unrestricted cash, future operating cash flow, committed refinancing, debt maturities, and remaining project capital expenditure.

Historical ROE is based on attributable net profit divided by average attributable net assets for the consolidated company. It is not calculated on the assumption that the 200,000-ton-per-year project operates at full capacity.

The 200,000-ton-per-year capacity cannot be converted into a reliable project net-profit figure from the disclosed information. A valid estimate requires throughput and utilization, product yields and prices, waste-plastics input economics, energy and other operating costs, depreciation, financing costs, and taxes.

A lower oil price does not mechanically determine Huicheng Environmental Protection's profit. Existing profits can come from catalyst sales, hazardous-waste treatment, and three-waste treatment, while the waste-plastics project's outcome depends on the spread between product prices and waste-plastics, energy, fixed, depreciation, and financing costs.

facts.statement: As of 2026-08-13, Wushang Group Co., Ltd. (000501.SZ) was described as using 30–40-year depreciation lives for its owned commercial-property buildings, while some comparable companies used 20–30 years.

(000501.SZ) had not publicly disclosed a complete asset-level dataset covering original cost, building-specific useful lives, residual rates, accumulated depreciation, remaining lives, and alternative-life calculations sufficient to quantify any potential under-depreciation or profit effect.

dependencies.requirement: Treat useful life as an asset-specific accounting estimate; do not infer that a 30–40-year life is unreasonable solely because some peers use 20–30 years.

Use the company's statements and the depreciation arithmetic only to identify a possible earnings effect; do not treat them as proof of manipulation or use them to quantify an amount without asset-level inputs.

Do not conclude that profit inflation, concealed state-asset deterioration, or duty dereliction occurred without evidence linking a specific duty, knowledge or notice, failure to act, and a resulting material misstatement or asset-loss risk.

answer_points.statement: A 30–40-year depreciation life is not inherently unreasonable merely because it exceeds the 20–30-year practice of some peers; reasonableness depends on each property's structure, age, design life, remaining rights, maintenance and renovation history, disposal experience, residual value, and impairment indicators.

A longer useful life can reduce current depreciation and increase reported profit and carrying value when other assumptions are unchanged, so it is a conditional accounting-estimate red flag if the estimated economic life exceeds the property's actual service life.

The company's self-reported consistency of policy and the stated impact of depreciation on a subsidiary's losses do not independently validate the reasonableness of the useful lives or exclude under-depreciation.

The available information is insufficient to establish that Wushang Group under-depreciated its properties, inflated profit, concealed actual state-asset deterioration, or had a governance-duty failure; it is also insufficient to quantify any such effect.

Accounting depreciation allocates historical cost, impairment addresses a decline in recoverable amount, and physical deterioration requires engineering or other asset-condition evidence; the depreciation life alone cannot prove that physical state-asset losses were concealed.

Further review should examine property-level useful-life assessments, residual rates, engineering evaluations, maintenance and renovation records, historical disposals, annual estimate reviews, impairment tests, audit or regulatory warnings, and documented corrective actions.

context_constraints.requirement: Apply the U.S. federal individual income-tax treatment for John and Jane as individual taxpayers mining and disposing of Monero and Bitcoin.
Distinguish mining income recognized at receipt, cryptocurrency tax basis, sale proceeds, capital gain or loss, and the separate tax liability.
Assume the stated prices are fair market values in U.S. dollars when received, Jane sells all five Bitcoin lots for $3,000 per Bitcoin, and there are no transaction fees.

facts.statement: IRS Notice 2014-21, Q&A 8–9, as applicable to 2017 U.S. federal tax treatment, provides that a miner generally includes the cryptocurrency's fair market value in U.S. dollars when received in gross income, and that amount generally becomes the cryptocurrency's tax basis.
In 2017, John received two Monero units through mining at stated receipt values of $20 and $23.
John's aggregate mining receipt value is $20 + $23 = $43.
In 2017, Jane received five mined Bitcoin lots of 0.02 Bitcoin each at stated receipt values of $28.00, $28.02, $28.10, $28.14, and $28.16.
Jane's aggregate mining receipt value is $28.00 + $28.02 + $28.10 + $28.14 + $28.16 = $140.42.
Jane later sold all 0.10 Bitcoin in 2017 at a stated price of $3,000 per Bitcoin.
Jane's sale proceeds are 0.10 Bitcoin × $3,000 per Bitcoin = $300.00.

dependencies.requirement: Apply the receipt-income and basis rule to John's $43 aggregate receipt value.
Treat mining income at receipt, tax basis, later sale gain, and tax liability as separate metrics; do not treat a taxable-income amount as the tax bill.
Apply the receipt-income and basis rule to Jane's $140.42 aggregate receipt value.
Compute Jane's later disposition gain as sale proceeds minus adjusted basis, using $140.42 as the aggregate basis and $300.00 as proceeds.

answer_points.statement: Mining generally creates taxable income when the cryptocurrency is successfully received, not only when it is later sold; the receipt value generally becomes the tax basis, and a later sale is a separate tax event.
For John, the two Monero units produce $43 of mining income and an initial aggregate basis of $43 upon receipt. Because he has not disposed of them, he has no recognized capital gain or loss yet.
For Jane, the five Bitcoin lots produce $140.42 of mining income and an aggregate basis of $140.42 upon receipt.
Jane's later sale produces $300.00 of proceeds and a separate capital gain of $159.58, so the stated basis and gain calculation is correct under the assumptions.

$140.42 and $159.58 are taxable-income or gain amounts, not the final tax bill. An exact tax liability requires filing status, applicable rates, deductible expenses, transaction fees, mining-business classification, self-employment-tax facts, and each lot's holding period.

If Jane held every lot for one year or less, the corresponding gain is generally short-term capital gain; a lot held for more than one year may receive long-term capital-gain treatment. Mining conducted as a trade or business may also create self-employment-tax liability.

numeric_targets.description: John's mining income upon receipt
Jane's mining income upon receipt
Jane's separate capital gain on the later sale

answer_points.statement: ChangXin Storage's potential listing should be analyzed separately from its capacity expansion: the listing itself has no inevitable direct operating effect on Longsys, although financing could indirectly support ChangXin's capacity, research, and supply capabilities.

The profitability effect is not unidirectionally positive: if industry supply grows faster than demand, storage selling prices may fall, competition may pass procurement savings to customers, and inventory write-down risk may increase, potentially offsetting lower wafer costs.

Longsys's future gross margin is more likely to remain cyclical and scenario-dependent than to rise linearly: in the short term it will depend on storage prices and inventory costs, while over the medium to long term enterprise, automotive-grade, embedded, and other higher-value-added products may reduce sensitivity to standardized-memory price swings.

Net margin will generally follow gross-margin direction but may fluctuate more because of research and development, selling and administrative expenses, share-based compensation, foreign-exchange and financing effects, inventory impairment, non-recurring items, and operating leverage.

Available evidence does not support a precise numerical forecast for Longsys's future gross or net margin; key monitoring indicators are ChangXin's actual commissioning and yield, Longsys's procurement amount or share, DRAM and product prices, inventory and write-down provisions, higher-value-added business mix, expense ratios, and operating cash flow.

facts.statement: At purchase, the hypothetical fixed-coupon bond has face value 100, a 10-year maturity, a 10% annual coupon, and a 12% annual yield to maturity.
Immediately after the second annual coupon payment, the hypothetical bond has eight remaining annual cash-flow dates.
At the new valuation date immediately after year 2, the hypothetical bond's current annual market yield is 8%.
At the new valuation date, the remaining cash flows are 10 at the end of each of years 1 through 7 and 110 at the end of year 8, in the normalized face-value units.
The current price is P2 = sum from k=1 to 8 of 10/(1.08)^k plus 100/(1.08)^8, equivalently the present value at 8% of the eight remaining cash flows.
The new Macaulay duration is [sum from k=1 to 8 of k times 10/(1.08)^k plus 8 times 100/(1.08)^8] divided by P2, measured in years.
With annual coupons and annual compounding, the new modified duration equals the new Macaulay duration divided by 1.08.

Use the price implied by the same remaining cash flows discounted at 8% as the denominator and valuation basis for Macaulay duration; do not use the original purchase price.
If modified duration is reported, derive it from Macaulay duration using the annual-compounding conversion D_mod = D_Mac/(1.08), and do not confuse the two measures.

answer_points.statement: Recalculate duration two years later using the eight remaining cash flows and the current 8% market yield.
The price used in the duration calculation must be the current price implied by discounting those same remaining cash flows at 8%, not the original purchase price.

The passage of time generally reduces duration by shortening the remaining maturity, while the yield decline from 12% to 8% generally increases duration for a conventional fixed-coupon bond; therefore, the net change must be calculated rather than inferred from elapsed time alone.

Macaulay duration is the present-value-weighted average time to the remaining cash flows; modified duration under annual compounding is Macaulay duration divided by 1.08 and approximates percentage price sensitivity to a small yield change.
If valuation occurs between coupon dates, use the exact times to each remaining cash flow and a consistently calculated dirty price including accrued interest.

The target level for frozen-product inventory cannot be determined from the reported fresh-product inventory figures; it requires a company-disclosed product breakdown or explicit management target.

A further 10% pork-price decline produces a conditional mechanical sensitivity of RMB 1.964 billion on the RMB 19.64 billion inventory base, but the actual additional impairment cannot be determined without item-level cost, net realizable value, selling and processing costs, and existing write-down allowances.

No reliable date can be given for the business or cash-flow recovery. The 2026 third-quarter report is the first monitoring window, while the 2026 annual report and dividend proposal are the principal confirmation window; the operating-cash-flow-to-profit ratio cannot be calculated or timed without same-period profit data.

numeric_targets.description: Conditional mechanical inventory value sensitivity from a 10% pork-price decline applied one-for-one to the RMB 19.64 billion inventory base

context_constraints.requirement: Compare a 2016 traditional IRA contribution with a 2016 Roth IRA contribution, while considering the user's planned Roth 401(k) contributions beginning in 2017.
Evaluate the tax decision over the stated approximately 40-year investment horizon.
Treat the traditional IRA contribution as deductible only if the user satisfies the applicable 2016 income, filing-status, and workplace-plan eligibility rules.
For an apples-to-apples comparison, assume comparable investment returns and either invest the traditional IRA tax savings or explicitly account for spending them.

facts.statement: For tax year 2016, the intended IRA contribution is USD 5,500.
For tax year 2016, the stated tax benefit from making the traditional IRA contribution is USD 1,000.
The user stated that they expect to open a Roth 401(k) in 2017 and currently have no IRA accounts.
The user stated that the relevant investment horizon is approximately 40 years.
For a deductible 2016 traditional IRA contribution, distributions are generally taxable, whereas qualified Roth IRA withdrawals are generally tax-free.
The stated USD 1,000 tax benefit divided by the USD 5,500 contribution equals 0.181818, or approximately 18.18%.
The stated USD 5,500 traditional IRA contribution less the USD 1,000 tax benefit implies an approximately USD 4,500 current after-tax cost.

dependencies.requirement: Use the approximately 18.18% implied current tax benefit as the break-even comparison with the future marginal tax rate on traditional IRA withdrawals.
Compare equal economic contributions; do not treat a USD 5,500 traditional contribution with the refund spent as equivalent to a USD 5,500 Roth contribution.
Use the planned Roth 401(k) and the stated refund only for practical tax-diversification and cash-flow considerations, not as an independent determination of the superior IRA type.

answer_points.statement: The USD 1,000 refund is primarily tax deferral rather than free money, because deductible traditional IRA withdrawals are generally taxed later.
The stated refund represents an implied current tax benefit of approximately 18.18% of the contribution.

Assuming full deductibility and comparable investment returns, a traditional IRA generally has the advantage when the future marginal withdrawal tax rate is below approximately 18.18%, while a Roth IRA generally has the advantage when it is above that level; they are broadly equivalent when the rates are equal and the tax savings are invested.

A fair comparison requires investing the traditional IRA tax savings or recognizing that the Roth IRA requires approximately USD 1,000 more current cash; spending the refund makes the comparison unequal.
The approximately 40-year horizon increases the dollar impact of the decision but does not by itself determine whether traditional or Roth is superior.

Choose traditional if the contribution is fully deductible, current cash flow matters, future retirement tax rates are expected to be lower, and the tax savings will be invested; choose Roth if future tax rates may be higher, current taxes are affordable, or greater tax-free retirement flexibility is preferred. Verify 2016 deductibility before relying on the USD 1,000 benefit.

numeric_targets.description: Implied current tax benefit as a percentage of the USD 5,500 contribution

It cannot be verified that high-value-added technology solutions have gross margins much higher than traditional distribution because comparable same-period, same-scope segment revenue, costs, and gross margins are unavailable.

facts.statement: Shenzhen Stock Exchange security code 300474.SZ corresponds to Jingjiawei (景嘉微).
On 2026-03-30, Jingjiawei (景嘉微) stated that its operations were normal and that it was continuing to perform delivery obligations under its contracts.
On 2026-03-30, Jingjiawei (景嘉微) also stated that contract execution involved multiple uncertainties and that the specific effects on future revenue and profit remained uncertain.

As of 2026-05-29, Jingjiawei (景嘉微) had not announced a further formal explanation specifically confirming an operational abnormality, an undisclosed reportable matter, or the cause of the share-price decline.

Use the 2026-03-30 company statement to support a qualified description of operations as publicly represented, while retaining the stated contract-related uncertainty.
Use the absence of a further formal announcement only to state that public evidence has not confirmed an abnormality; do not convert it into proof that no undisclosed matter exists.

Based on the available public evidence, no undisclosed reportable abnormality has been confirmed; however, the evidence is insufficient to conclude that no undisclosed matter exists.
The share-price decline alone cannot establish an operational abnormality, an undisclosed material matter, or a unique or primary cause of the decline.
Further assessment should rely on Jingjiawei's formal announcements and any Shenzhen Stock Exchange inquiries and responses.

context_constraints.requirement: Compare a traditional employer-sponsored 401(k) with a taxable brokerage account holding comparable index funds.
Evaluate investment growth and pre-tax or after-tax value, while excluding liquidity and withdrawal-access considerations.
Assume comparable employer cost, investment returns, fees unless otherwise noted, and that any increased employer contribution is lawful, plan-permitted, and vested.

facts.statement: As of 2022-01-04, traditional 401(k) assets generally compound without annual taxation of dividends or realized gains, while distributions are generally taxable as ordinary income.

As of 2022-01-04, salary invested in a taxable brokerage account is reduced by applicable income and payroll taxes before investment, and dividends and realized gains may create ongoing tax drag; the original cost basis is generally not taxed again when sold.
As of 2022-01-04, a given index fund does not earn a higher underlying market return merely because it is held in a 401(k) rather than a taxable brokerage account.

As of 2022-01-04, an employee election to exchange currently available salary for a retirement contribution may be treated as a salary-reduction elective deferral rather than as a genuine nonelective employer contribution.

As of 2022-01-04, employer and employee 401(k) contributions are subject to plan-document provisions, combined annual limits, compensation and allocation rules, and applicable nondiscrimination or testing requirements.

As of 2022-01-04, the after-tax comparison depends on contribution and withdrawal tax rates, taxable-fund distributions and turnover, capital-gains treatment, 401(k) fees, and employer-contribution vesting.

dependencies.requirement: Use the tax-treatment comparison and equal underlying investment return to support the conclusion that the 401(k) will ordinarily have a larger pre-withdrawal balance under comparable conditions.
Use tax rates, fees, taxable-account tax drag, and vesting to qualify the conclusion; do not state that the 401(k) is automatically superior for after-tax spending value.

Distinguish a genuine employer contribution from an employee salary-reduction elective deferral, and account for plan-specific limits and compliance rules; do not assume that salary can simply be relabeled as an employer contribution.

answer_points.statement: Holding the same index fund in a 401(k) does not increase its market return; the potential advantage comes from investing more initially and avoiding annual tax drag.

A traditional 401(k) will ordinarily produce a larger pre-tax account balance than investing the after-tax remainder of salary in a taxable brokerage account, assuming comparable investments, employer cost, fees, and lawful vested contributions.
The 401(k) advantage is tax deferral rather than tax exemption because distributions are generally taxable as ordinary income.
The arrangement is not automatically better after tax because the outcome depends on contribution and withdrawal tax rates, taxable-account tax drag, capital-gains treatment, fees, and vesting.

An employee may not be able to elect to receive less available salary and have the difference simply labeled an employer contribution; the arrangement may be treated as an elective deferral and must satisfy applicable plan and nondiscrimination rules.

Before changing salary, the employee should obtain confirmation from the plan administrator or a qualified ERISA or tax professional; no specific annual contribution limit should be assumed without plan-specific verification.

context_constraints.requirement: Analyze a typical U.S. married couple filing a joint federal income-tax return.
Compare wages attributable to tax year 2019 with wages attributable to tax year 2020, based on payment or availability timing.
Compare final federal tax liability, not Form W-4 withholding.
For the wage-allocation comparison, assume the same deductions, credits, benefits, and other income, with ordinary wages and both spouses below the Social Security wage ceiling.

facts.statement: For a typical U.S. married couple filing jointly, federal income-tax liability for tax years 2019 and 2020 is not determined solely by whether a spouse was employed or unemployed on December 31.

For U.S. wage income, compensation paid or made available in December 2019 generally belongs to tax year 2019, while compensation first paid or made available in January 2020 generally belongs to tax year 2020.

For a U.S. married couple filing jointly in tax years 2019 and 2020, regular federal income-tax brackets generally apply to the couple's combined taxable income, subject to deductions, credits, benefits, and other income.
For U.S. tax years 2019 and 2020, Form W-4 withholding is a prepayment and does not determine final federal income-tax liability.

For the stated U.S. wage examples in tax years 2019 and 2020, both spouses remain below the Social Security wage ceiling, so employee Social Security and Medicare taxes generally total the same under either wage allocation.
The first wage allocation is USD 100,000 for one spouse plus USD 0 for the other spouse, equal to USD 100,000 of combined wages.
The second wage allocation is USD 50,000 for one spouse plus USD 50,000 for the other spouse, equal to USD 100,000 of combined wages.

dependencies.requirement: Use the equal combined wage totals and joint-return treatment to conclude that regular federal income-tax liability is generally the same only when deductions, credits, benefits, other income, and taxable-income treatment are otherwise identical.
Determine whether December work affects the 2019 or 2020 return from the wage payment or availability date, not merely from the first day of employment.
Do not treat different W-4 withholding amounts as different final tax liabilities.
Limit the equal payroll-tax observation to the stated wage levels; do not extend it to earnings that exceed the Social Security wage ceiling for an individual worker.

answer_points.statement: Being employed or unemployed on December 31 does not by itself change a married couple's federal income-tax liability.

If the wife's December wages are paid or made available in December 2019, they generally belong on the 2019 return; if first paid or made available in January 2020, they generally belong on the 2020 return. A December signing bonus may also affect the comparison.

Under the stated assumptions, USD 100,000 earned by one spouse and USD 0 by the other generally produces the same regular federal income-tax liability as USD 50,000 earned by each spouse, because combined taxable income is the same.
W-4 withholding may differ between the two arrangements, but withholding is only a prepayment and does not determine the final tax due.

Neither December nor January is categorically tax-optimal. December work generally should not be rejected solely because the wife is employed on December 31, while starting in January may defer those wages into 2020 and may be preferable if the household's 2020 tax circumstances are more favorable.

The decision also depends on payment timing, whether January preserves or forfeits compensation, household income in both years, income-dependent credits and benefits, retirement benefits, deductions, and state or local tax rules.

context_constraints.requirement: The security is not identified by name or ticker; recommendations must therefore remain generic and must not assert issuer-specific fundamentals.
Assess the user-specified current holding snapshot and subsequent actions, not a multi-period financial report.
Use only the 500-share position and exclude commissions, taxes, dividends, other holdings, and other transactions.
Treat prices as RMB per share, position size as shares, totals as RMB, and returns as percentages.
Treat RMB 8.39 as the current price and RMB 9.39 as the initial per-share cost; do not treat the historical cost as evidence that the price will recover.

facts.statement: For the user-specified unidentified stock in the current holding snapshot, the position is 500 shares, the current price is RMB 8.39 per share, and the initial cost is RMB 9.39 per share.
Initial total cost = RMB 9.39 per share × 500 shares = RMB 4,695.
Current market value = RMB 8.39 per share × 500 shares = RMB 4,195.
Unrealized profit or loss = RMB 4,195 − RMB 4,695 = negative RMB 500, representing an unrealized loss of RMB 500.
Holding return = negative RMB 500 ÷ RMB 4,695 × 100% = approximately negative 10.65%.

dependencies.requirement: Use the specified share count, current price, and initial cost to calculate the position's cost, market value, unrealized loss, and return.
Calculate the return against initial total cost and exclude commissions, taxes, dividends, and other positions.
Use the quantified loss only to frame risk-management options, not as evidence that the stock should recover or that a specific trade is required.

answer_points.statement: The position has an initial total cost of RMB 4,695, a current market value of RMB 4,195, an unrealized loss of RMB 500, and an approximate holding return of -10.65%.

Continuing to hold may be appropriate only if the original investment thesis remains valid, the funds are not needed soon, the position size is manageable, and further losses are acceptable; predefined exit conditions should be established.

Reducing or stopping the position, either all at once or in stages, is more appropriate if the investment thesis has failed, the position is near the investor's maximum tolerable loss, or further volatility cannot be tolerated.

Do not add merely because the price fell from RMB 9.39 to RMB 8.39. Adding should require a revalidated thesis, sufficient idle funds, a tolerable total position size, and a predefined maximum loss if the decline continues.

Given the absence of issuer-specific fundamentals, price history, position concentration, and personal risk tolerance, the prudent sequence is to revalidate the holding rationale first, then choose conditional holding, staged reduction, or only limited staged adding; no unconditional buy or sell instruction is supported.

numeric_targets.description: Unrealized loss on the 500-share position
Holding return relative to initial total cost

context_constraints.requirement: Treat the investment as an Ireland-domiciled Vanguard S&P 500 ETF held by a Netherlands-resident investor; the exact ISIN and share class are unspecified.
Measure the incremental annual holding cost as unrecoverable dividend-tax drag relative to investment value, separate from capital gains.
Separate withholding incurred inside the fund on dividends received from US companies from any withholding on distributions paid by the Irish fund to the investor, and do not double-count them.
Treat the 20% Irish rate as a conditional assumption until the fund documentation, distribution statement, and Dutch credit or reclaim treatment establish that it applies and is unrecoverable.

facts.statement: As of 2019-07-18, the investment described is an Ireland-domiciled Vanguard S&P 500 ETF held by a Netherlands-resident investor; the exact ISIN and share class are unspecified.

As of 2019-07-18, the 20% Irish dividend-tax rate is the rate assumed for the conditional calculation, not an established applicable and unrecoverable investor-level rate for the unspecified ETF share class.

As of 2019-07-18, dividend withholding can arise at two distinct stages: when US companies pay dividends to the Irish fund and when the Irish fund distributes income to the Netherlands-resident investor.
For EUR 1.00 of taxable dividend, a 20% unrecoverable investor-level tax rate produces EUR 0.20 of tax: EUR 1.00 × 0.20 = EUR 0.20.
For an ETF distribution yield y and unrecoverable investor-level tax rate r, annual investor-level tax drag equals y × r of investment value.

Approximate annual all-in drag equals the ETF TER plus distribution yield × unrecoverable investor-level tax rate, with material tracking, trading, custody, and rebalancing costs considered separately.
The incremental tax drag versus a direct portfolio equals ETF distribution yield × (the ETF's unrecoverable effective tax rate − the direct portfolio's unrecoverable effective tax rate).

dependencies.requirement: Keep fund-level withholding separate from investor-level withholding and do not add both unless they are confirmed to be separate, unrecoverable costs.
Present the 20% calculation only conditionally; do not state that 20% is the verified Irish withholding rate for the investor's ETF distribution.
Use the calculated investor-level tax drag as an input to the approximate all-in annual cost, while excluding capital gains from the yield multiplication.
Compare the ETF with a homemade portfolio using the difference between their unrecoverable effective dividend-tax rates, then add the ETF TER and other material cost differences.

answer_points.statement: Do not automatically apply Ireland's headline 20% dividend-tax rate: the applicable withholding and its recoverability depend on the fund, share class, investor documentation, and Dutch tax-credit or reclaim treatment.
If 20% is both withheld and unrecoverable, annual investor-level tax drag is distribution yield × 20%; the tax is charged on dividends, not on the full investment or on capital gains.

The approximate all-in annual drag is TER + distribution yield × the applicable unrecoverable investor-level tax rate, with material tracking, trading, custody, and rebalancing costs treated separately.

Distinguish withholding borne inside the Irish fund from withholding on distributions paid to the investor, and avoid mechanically adding them because some tax may already be reflected in the fund's return.

Against a homemade direct portfolio, the relevant additional tax cost is ETF distribution yield × (ETF unrecoverable effective tax rate − direct-portfolio unrecoverable effective tax rate), plus the ETF's TER and other material cost differences.

A specific annual loss cannot be determined without the ETF's exact ISIN and share class, distribution yield, TER, verified withholding, Dutch creditability or reclaim treatment, and comparable direct-portfolio tax rate; these should be checked in the fund disclosures, broker statement, and Dutch tax return.

numeric_targets.description: Conditional tax loss on EUR 1.00 of taxable dividend if the unrecoverable investor-level rate is 20%
numeric_targets.unit: EUR per EUR 1.00 of taxable dividend

context_constraints.requirement: Use Beijing Shenzhou Taiyue Software Co., Ltd. (300002.SZ) as the company and Mao Dajun as its chairman and president.
Keep Mao Dajun's 2024 and 2025 remuneration separate from the 2023 employee stock ownership plan and its 2023–2024 performance-assessment periods.

Distinguish reported annual cash remuneration, employee stock ownership plan transfer prices, restricted-stock grant prices, revenue, net profit, and stock price; equity-incentive conditions must not be treated as a cash-remuneration formula.
Express remuneration in RMB million or RMB yuan, share prices in RMB per share, and share quantities in shares.

facts.statement: Beijing Shenzhou Taiyue Software Co., Ltd. (300002.SZ) identifies Mao Dajun as its chairman and president.
Media reports based on the company's senior-executive remuneration list state that Mao Dajun's reported remuneration was RMB 9.715 million for 2024 and RMB 8.618 million for 2025.

As of 2026-07-15, Beijing Shenzhou Taiyue Software Co., Ltd. had not publicly disclosed a complete, independently verifiable formula specifying the fixed-pay and performance-pay components, decision process, indicator weights, targets, completion rates, or revenue, net-profit, and stock-price linkage for Mao Dajun's annual cash remuneration.

Beijing Shenzhou Taiyue Software Co., Ltd.'s 2023 employee stock ownership plan set a first unlocking-period condition of at least 15% net-profit growth in 2023, and a second unlocking-period condition of at least 25% net-profit growth in 2024 or combined net profit of at least RMB 1.301 billion for 2023–2024.

Under Beijing Shenzhou Taiyue Software Co., Ltd.'s 2023 employee stock ownership plan, the transfer price was RMB 2.00 per share, Mao Dajun's holding cap was 2.05 million shares, and his share represented 21.79% of the plan's total amount.

Under Beijing Shenzhou Taiyue Software Co., Ltd.'s 2023 restricted-stock incentive plan, the grant price was RMB 5.00 per share under a self-determined pricing method, and Mao Dajun was proposed to receive approximately 6.397823 million shares, representing 68.01% of the total proposed grant.

The Shenzhen Stock Exchange sent Beijing Shenzhou Taiyue Software Co., Ltd. a letter requesting explanations of the basis and reasonableness of the employee stock ownership plan's transfer price and performance standards, including whether利益输送 (improper transfer of benefits) might be involved; the inquiry itself was not a finding that such conduct had occurred.

dependencies.requirement: Separate annual cash remuneration from the employee stock ownership plan and restricted-stock incentive plan; do not infer that the latter plans' prices or performance conditions constitute the cash-remuneration formula.
Compare 2024 and 2025 remuneration only with their respective reporting years, and apply the employee stock ownership plan's performance conditions only to its specified 2023–2024 assessment periods.

Conclude that the cash-remuneration linkage is not publicly verifiable while separately recognizing the explicit net-profit conditions in the employee stock ownership plan; do not treat regulatory questions as an established violation.

answer_points.statement: The description of Mao Dajun's annual remuneration as close to RMB 10 million is accurate mainly for 2024, when reported remuneration was RMB 9.715 million; his reported 2025 remuneration was lower at RMB 8.618 million.

Available public information does not disclose enough detail to determine how the annual cash remuneration was set, including the responsible decision-makers, fixed-versus-performance components, indicators, weights, targets, or calculation formula.

There is no publicly verifiable evidence of a fixed formula linking Mao Dajun's annual cash remuneration to company revenue, net profit, or stock price. Conversely, the available evidence is also insufficient to conclude that the remuneration was formally independent of all performance measures.

The 2023 employee stock ownership plan was a separate equity arrangement with explicit net-profit performance conditions, whereas the restricted-stock incentive plan used a separate grant-price and grant-quantity arrangement; neither arrangement proves that the same conditions governed annual cash remuneration.

The RMB 2.00 per-share employee stock ownership plan transfer price and RMB 5.00 per-share restricted-stock grant price describe equity-pricing arrangements, not stock-price performance conditions. No clear term was identified making stock-price changes an annual cash-pay or equity-unlocking metric.

Past declines in revenue, net profit, or stock price cannot by themselves establish the cash-remuneration formula, prove that remuneration was unlinked to performance, or determine whether the relevant shares had become unconditionally vested.

context_constraints.requirement: Assess the fiscal position of the United States federal government, not state, local, household, or corporate finances.
Distinguish the debt stock, annual total deficit, primary deficit, net interest, and debt or interest measured as a share of GDP or federal revenue.
Use federal-budget accounting and distinguish temporary deficit flows from their lasting effects on debt held by the public.

facts.statement: For the United States federal budget, the annual total deficit is approximately the primary deficit plus net interest; the national debt is the accumulated stock of prior borrowing.
The United States federal net-interest figures used for FY2019 and FY2024 are USD 375 billion and USD 880 billion, respectively.
The increase in United States federal net interest from FY2019 to FY2024 is USD 880 billion minus USD 375 billion, or USD 505 billion.

The United States federal FY2024 deficit was approximately 6.6% of GDP, the FY2025 projected deficit was approximately 6.2% of GDP, and net interest was approximately 3.1% of GDP in 2024 and was projected at 4.1% of GDP in 2035.
United States debt held by the public was projected at approximately 99.9% of GDP in 2025 and 118.5% of GDP in 2035.
The first approximately USD 2.6 trillion round of United States pandemic relief was concentrated in 2020 and 2021, with approximately USD 2.3 trillion spent in 2020 and USD 0.3 trillion in 2021.
United States pandemic borrowing incurred in 2020-2021 remains part of the federal debt stock and can generate later interest costs.

United States infrastructure, CHIPS, and Inflation Reduction Act measures enacted in 2021-2022 use multiple fiscal instruments, including appropriations, grants, loans, loan guarantees, and tax credits, with fiscal effects distributed across multiple years.
Higher United States federal interest costs during FY2019-FY2024 reflect both higher borrowing rates and the larger debt stock, with Treasury debt repricing as securities mature.

dependencies.requirement: Use the FY2019 and FY2024 net-interest amounts to establish the USD 505 billion increase; do not treat this increase alone as a complete causal or sustainability analysis.
Assess fiscal sustainability with the primary balance, net interest, deficit, and debt relative to GDP or revenue, rather than with nominal deficit levels alone.
The interest increase can exceed an approximately USD 200 billion deviation from a chosen deficit trend only conditionally on that trend being valid and the fiscal-year data being comparable.
Treat direct pandemic relief as largely expired while still recognizing that the borrowing and associated interest effects remain.
Do not treat a multiyear industrial-policy headline amount as one year's spending or assume that onshoring automatically offsets its federal budget cost.
Use the projected debt and interest ratios to distinguish an immediate financing crisis from a worsening medium- and long-term structural fiscal problem.

answer_points.statement: The United States does not appear to face an immediate sovereign-financing or ordinary near-term default crisis, but its fiscal policy presents a genuine and worsening medium- and long-term structural problem.

The increase in net interest can more than account for the approximately USD 200 billion FY2024 deviation from the stated pre-pandemic deficit trend in a narrow accounting comparison, but only conditionally on the unavailable graph and trend specification being valid.

Rising interest is not a complete explanation of the fiscal trajectory: it reflects both higher rates and accumulated debt, while primary deficits and prior policy choices contribute to the debt and later interest burden.
Direct pandemic relief was largely a temporary deficit flow concentrated in 2020-2021, but the resulting debt remains and continues to affect interest costs.

Industrial-policy costs are spread across multiple years and fiscal instruments; they were not all already spent, and possible onshoring tax gains cannot be assumed to provide a dollar-for-dollar offset.

Calling the debt crisis entirely fake is too strong, while claiming imminent insolvency or that one spending category is the only solution is also unsupported; stabilization could combine spending changes, higher revenue, faster growth, and lower borrowing costs.

context_constraints.requirement: The date field and time window must be explicitly defined. If "last month" means one rolling calendar month ending at 2026-06-02 07:46:41.501 UTC, the inclusive UTC window is 2026-05-02 07:46:41.501 through 2026-06-02 07:46:41.501.
Verify whether the platform uses a rolling calendar month, a fixed-day window, a natural month, or recent trading days, including timezone, date granularity, and boundary inclusion.

The filter must distinguish the rating value "Buy (买入)", the relevant announcement or rating date, the forward-adjusted target price (前复权目标价), and the closing price (收盘价), and must preserve the parentheses in the upside formula.
The target price and closing price must use the same currency and compatible price basis; the 0.4 threshold must be interpreted as a ratio rather than a percentage value of 40.
The rating, date, target price, and closing price should be associated with the same security and, where applicable, the same rating or research-report record.

facts.statement: For a non-null closing price greater than zero, (forward-adjusted target price - closing price) / closing price > 0.4 is equivalent to forward-adjusted target price > 1.4 times the closing price.
If the period is defined as one rolling calendar month ending at 2026-06-02 07:46:41.501 UTC, the corresponding inclusive UTC interval is 2026-05-02 07:46:41.501 to 2026-06-02 07:46:41.501.
In SQL-like three-valued filtering, an arithmetic expression involving a null target price or null closing price evaluates to null, and a null comparison with 0.4 is not true.
An exact equality predicate for the stored rating string "Buy (买入)" does not match alternative stored values such as "Strong Buy", "Outperform", "Buy", or strings containing extra whitespace.
An upside comparison between a target price and a closing price requires the same security, compatible currency, comparable date basis, and compatible adjustment basis.

dependencies.requirement: Validate that both prices are non-null and that the closing price is greater than zero before interpreting or applying the upside threshold.
Use the stated interval only if the platform defines "last month" as a rolling calendar month in UTC; otherwise recompute the interval using the platform's period and timezone rules.

Confirm the actual rating enumeration and verify that the rating, date, target price, and closing price refer to compatible records and price definitions; do not treat a different rating label or an incompatible price basis as a valid match.

answer_points.statement: Zero matches do not by themselves prove that no stock satisfies the economic conditions. Without field samples and intermediate hit counts, the unique root cause cannot be determined; the true intersection may simply be empty or the filter may contain a field, linkage, null-handling, enumeration, date, or unit problem.

The intended logic should be written explicitly as: rating = "Buy (买入)" AND the relevant date is within the defined window AND target price IS NOT NULL AND closing price IS NOT NULL AND closing price > 0 AND ((forward-adjusted target price - closing price) / closing price) > 0.4.

The announcement date may be a company-announcement date rather than a rating, research-report, target-price, or rating-change date. The rating, target price, and date may also come from different records, eliminating the intersection.

Other common causes are an exact-match mismatch in the rating enumeration, missing target prices, incompatible security/currency/date/adjustment bases, or confusion between a ratio displayed as 0.xx and a percentage displayed as xx%.

Diagnose the zero-result stage with a funnel: count each individual condition, each pairwise intersection, and the full intersection; then inspect raw rating, date, record identifier, target price, closing price, price dates, adjustment types, calculated upside, and TRUE/FALSE/NULL status.

facts.statement: As of 2026-07-20, Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 002011 identifies Dunan Environment (002011.SZ), and the disclosed undertaking to avoid horizontal competition was given by Gree Electric Appliances, Inc. of Zhuhai (000651.SZ), not automatically by every Gree-affiliated entity.

As of 2026-07-20, no publicly disclosed company announcement, formal institutional research record, or identifiable primary statement had confirmed all of the reported elements that Gree would invest RMB 800 million in a South China liquid-cooling supporting base intended to supplement Dunan Environment's liquid-cooling components.

In the undertaking disclosed on 2022-01-13, Gree Electric Appliances stated that, subject to feasible conditions and the interests of both parties, it would resolve existing competition involving commercial air-conditioning products and certain HVAC equipment through restructuring, asset disposal, equity or operating entrustment, or assignment of new business opportunities to Dunan Environment within five years after completion of the acquisition.

The undertaking disclosed on 2022-01-13 states that if Gree Electric Appliances or another subsidiary obtains a business opportunity constituting substantial horizontal competition with Dunan Environment, it must notify Dunan Environment in writing, subject to an exception for certain minority equity financial-investment opportunities that do not create control or significant influence.

In a disclosure dated 2026-01-07, Dunan Environment reported that Gree Electric Appliances' undertaking was being normally performed and that no breach or overdue performance had occurred; in a company secretary response dated 2025-01-08, Dunan Environment likewise stated that the undertaking was being continuously performed and remained within its term.

In a Gree Electric Appliances company secretary response dated 2025-12-12, Gree described its liquid-cooling business as focused on system solutions and integrated equipment delivery, while Dunan Environment was described as focusing on supporting components, including electronic expansion valves, microchannel heat exchangers, and liquid-cooling plates.

dependencies.requirement: Apply the undertaking only after determining whether the actual investment party is Gree Electric Appliances or a subsidiary covered by the undertaking; do not treat every Gree-named entity as automatically bound.

Compare the actual project party, products, and business opportunity with the undertaking's scope of substantial competition and its notification mechanisms; do not equate all liquid-cooling activities or component relationships with a breach.

answer_points.statement: The report that Gree will invest RMB 800 million in a South China liquid-cooling supporting base to supplement Dunan Environment's liquid-cooling components is currently unverified and should not be treated as an established fact.
The lack of reliable confirmation does not by itself prove that the report is false.

The relevant undertaking is principally Gree Electric Appliances' undertaking, covering specified existing competition, substantial competing business opportunities, and prescribed resolution or written-notification arrangements.

Gree's system-solution and integrated-equipment business and Dunan Environment's liquid-cooling-component business have been publicly described as differentiated, although that distinction alone does not resolve every future competition question.

Based on the available evidence, the reported investment cannot be found to violate the undertaking because the investment party, actual products, substantial-competition status, and required notification or business-opportunity arrangements have not been reliably established.

A further compliance determination would require formal confirmation of the investment party and project scope, followed by comparison with the undertaking and verification of any required notification or opportunity-allocation procedures.

facts.statement: iFlytek Co., Ltd. (科大讯飞) (002230.SZ) is the company corresponding to Shenzhen Stock Exchange code 002230.

iFlytek's reported research and development expenses were RMB 3.111 billion in 2022, RMB 3.481 billion in 2023, RMB 3.892 billion in 2024, and RMB 3.188 billion for January–September 2025; the research and development expense ratio remained above 16% during January–September 2025.

In explanations concerning profit trends, iFlytek attributed the divergence between revenue and non-recurring-item-excluded net profit attributable to shareholders to increased research and development investment as well as higher selling expenses and accounts-receivable impairment losses; the 2023 decline was also associated with domestic-substitution investment, iFlytek Spark large-model research and development, and business-structure adjustments, while the 2024 recovery was associated with large-model commercialization.

An external review of iFlytek's third-quarter 2025 report stated that the research and development expense ratio was 18.76% for the first three quarters of 2025, versus 20.45% for the same period of 2024.

As of 2026-06-17, iFlytek had not publicly disclosed a specific list of non-core or slow-payback research projects to be cut, an implementation timetable, an annual research and development expense cap, or a quantified expense-reduction target; its public statements continued to emphasize high-intensity research and development focused on large models and domestic computing infrastructure.

If revenue, gross margin, other expenses, impairment losses, and income tax are unchanged, reducing immediately stoppable research and development expenditures that are expensed in the current period lowers current-period expense and increases current-period pretax profit; reducing capitalized research and development expenditures does not necessarily create an equivalent immediate profit increase, and previously capitalized assets may subsequently generate amortization or impairment.

dependencies.requirement: Apply all historical data, accounting analysis, and management-plan conclusions to iFlytek (002230.SZ), not to another issuer.

Do not equate research and development expense with non-recurring-item-excluded net profit or current-period net profit, and distinguish expensed research and development from capitalized development expenditures.

Use the immediate profit-improvement conclusion only conditionally: it applies primarily to current-period expensed research and development under otherwise-unchanged conditions, and must not be presented as sustainable earnings elasticity.

Use the historical expense data and disclosed profit drivers to support that research and development pressured profit but was not the sole cause; treat the lower expense ratio as an observation, not as evidence of a formal project-cutting plan.

answer_points.statement: Reducing current-period expensed research and development can relatively quickly increase current-period pretax profit, and usually current-period net profit after tax, if other relevant conditions remain unchanged.

This effect is primarily a short-term accounting reduction in expense and does not by itself establish sustainable earnings elasticity; the impact will also depend on taxes, one-off adjustments, commercialization, revenue, gross margin, and subsequent impairment or amortization.

The available disclosures support that high research and development investment pressured iFlytek's profitability, but selling expenses, accounts-receivable impairment losses, business-structure changes, and commercialization timing were also material factors.

The relevant disclosure indicates that research and development expense intensity had declined by the first three quarters of 2025, but this observation does not establish that management had adopted a plan to cut non-core or slow-payback projects.

As of 2026-06-17, available public disclosures had not confirmed a specific project-cutting list, implementation timetable, annual research and development budget cap, or quantified cost-reduction target from management.

A reliable estimate of profit uplift or realization speed is not possible without project-level information on the expensed proportion, exit costs, and effects on future revenue and commercialization; focusing research and development and improving commercialization is more durable than simply reducing its absolute amount.

Under the applicable inventory accounting rules as of 2026-07-19, inventory is measured at the lower of cost and net realizable value; a recovery in net realizable value may reverse previously recognized inventory write-downs only within the amount previously recognized, and cannot remeasure inventory above its original cost.

Under the applicable inventory accounting rules as of 2026-07-19, net realizable value is estimated selling price less costs of completion, selling expenses, and related taxes; inventory covered by a fixed-price contract also requires consideration of the contract price rather than merely the spot-market price.

As of 2026-07-19, equipment purchased for resale may be classified as inventory, whereas equipment used to provide computing services may be classified as property, plant and equipment or construction in progress; a market-price increase ordinarily does not directly increase the carrying amount of property, plant and equipment measured under the cost model.
